```kotlin
    category = EqualCategory.Others,
    title = "Dr. Mehta's Clinic Appointment",
    lines = listOf(
        ActionCardLine("Tomorrow, 9:00 AM"),
        ActionCardLine("Bring previous medical reports", ActionCardTone.Tertiary),
    ),
    timestamp = "03:21",
    actions = listOf(
        ActionCardAction("Confirm", emoji = "👍", onClick = {}),
        ActionCardAction("Edit", emoji = "✏️", onClick = {}),
    ),
)
```

Example: Instruction saved
```tsx
<ActionCard icon="instructions" title="Instruction saved"
  details={instructionLines('Delivery agents call', 'Ask them to leave parcels with security')}
  time="03:21" actions={[{ label: 'Edit rule', emoji: '✏️' }]} />
```
```kotlin
ActionCard(
    icon = EqualIcons.Instructions,
    title = "Instruction saved",
    lines = instructionLines("Delivery agents call", "Ask them to leave parcels with security"),
    timestamp = "03:21",
    actions = listOf(ActionCardAction("Edit rule", emoji = "✏️", onClick = {})),
)
```

Example: Instruction (body only)
```tsx
<ActionCardBody icon="instructions" title="Instructions"
  details={instructionLines('Bank calls come', 'Tell callers I’ll call back after 6 PM')}
  time="03:21" />
```
```kotlin
ActionCardBody(
    icon = EqualIcons.Instructions,
    title = "Instructions",
    lines = instructionLines("Bank calls come", "Tell callers I’ll call back after 6 PM"),
    timestamp = "03:21",
)
```

#### Assistant toggle (`assistant-toggle`)

The card at the top of Chats and the You tab that turns the AI assistant on or off, with the mascot dimming when it is off.

- React: `import { AssistantToggle } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `AssistantToggleCard`
- Tokens: `assistant-toggle/bg`, `bg/surface`, `stroke/subtle`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `button/primary`, `button/disabled`, `action/stroke/unread`
- Source: §3 Assistant Availability Toggle

Do: Put it directly under the top bar on Chats (HomeHeader does this) and first under YOUR ASSISTANT on the You tab. Let the default copy explain the state: on manages unknown calls, off lets them ring normally.

Don't: Don't crop or replace the mascot; it dims itself when off. Don't add a Save button; the change applies immediately.

Anatomy:
1. Card: Rounded card whose fill shows on or off. (min height 64 (web) / height 64 (Compose) · padding 12 10 12 12 · radius xl (20) · on: assistant-toggle/bg with an action/stroke/unread glow at each end · off: bg/surface + 1 px stroke/subtle)
2. Mascot: Robot mascot (or the 3D phone experiment) that greys out when off. (Mascot / EqualMascot 36 · off: greyscale, opacity 0.7 · phone art: Asset assistant-phone 36, opacity 0.5 when off)
3. Title: States on or off. (Text subheading · text/primary · one line · "AI Assistant is On / Off")
4. Description: What the state means. (Text caption Regular · text/secondary · one line, ellipsis)
5. Switch: The control. (gap 10 (web) / 12 (Compose) · track 40 × 24 · thumb 18 · on button/primary, thumb text/on-action · off button/disabled, white thumb)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Only the switch is interactive: <button role="switch">; the mascot is role=img. Android: The whole card is toggleable(role = Role.Switch); the inner EqualSwitch has onCheckedChange = null, so it is visual only.
- Name. Web: Switch aria-label "AI Assistant"; the mascot reads "Equal assistant"; the title and description are read as text but are not tied to the switch. Android: The merged card reads the mascot ("Equal assistant"), the title and the description.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to the switch; Space / Enter toggles; the change applies at once. Android: TalkBack: one stop for the card, double-tap to toggle.
- Touch target. Web: The 40 × 24 switch uses eq-touch for a 48 px hit area; the rest of the card is not tappable. Android: The whole 64 dp card is the target.
- Contrast. Web: Title text/primary 12.5:1 and description text/secondary 5.7:1 on both fills. Switch tracks are weak: off #DDDDDD on white 1.36:1 (dark #444444 on #1F1F1F 1.7:1); on is brand green #00B140, 2.85:1 (accepted brand decision). Android: Same tokens, same ratios.
- State. Web: aria-checked on the switch, and the title spells On / Off, so not colour alone. Android: toggleable exposes checked; the title and description change with the state.
- Motion. Web: Track, thumb (500 ms), card and mascot transitions go to 0 ms under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: EqualSwitch animates over 500 ms, 0 ms when Remove animations is on; the card fill changes instantly.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Switch off track button/disabled #DDDDDD on white is 1.36:1 (dark 1.7:1), below 3:1 for a control boundary (Switch.css, EqualSwitch.kt); the title does state On / Off.
- Accepted brand decision: the on track is button/primary #00B140 (2.85:1 on white), just under 3:1 for a control (Switch.css, EqualSwitch.kt).
- AssistantToggleCard fixes the card at height(64.dp), so at large font scales the one-line title and description no longer fit and get clipped; web uses min-height (HomeChrome.kt).

Example: Interactive
```tsx
const [on, setOn] = useState(true);

<AssistantToggle on={on} onChange={setOn} />
```
```kotlin
var on by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }
AssistantToggleCard(checked = on, onCheckedChange = { on = it })
```

Example: On and off
```tsx
<AssistantToggle on />
<AssistantToggle on={false} />
```
```kotlin
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)) {
    AssistantToggleCard(checked = true, onCheckedChange = {})
    AssistantToggleCard(checked = false, onCheckedChange = {})
}
```

#### Feedback card (`feedback-card`)

The post-call card that asks the user to rate the call from one to five stars and share feedback.

- React: `import { FeedbackCard } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `FeedbackCard`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `rating/star-filled`, `rating/star-empty`, `text/placeholder`, `stroke/subtle`, `text/action`
- Source: §13 Feedback Card

Do: Show it once, right after the call summary, indented to line up with the summary bubble. Keep the question short and about the call itself.

Don't: Don't add a text field to the card; Share Feedback opens the next step. Don't use emoji or images for the stars; they are coded.

Anatomy:
1. Card: White card for the rating. (width 246 · bg/surface · radius md (12) · overflow hidden)
2. Question: Asks the user to rate the call. (Text body1 · text/primary · padding 12 10 10)
3. Stars: Five tappable stars. (web: Icon star 32, gap 8, 40 × 48 touch cells · Compose: Icon star 28 centred in 48 dp cells, no gap · filled rating/star-filled · empty outline rating/star-empty)
4. Divider: Separates the rating from the action. (1 px stroke/subtle)
5. Share Feedback: Sends the rating. (40 high (web, TextButton with 48 touch area) / 48 dp (Compose) · Text button text/action · chevron-right 18 (web) / 16 (Compose))

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Stars are <button role="radio"> in a role="radiogroup" aria-label "Rating"; Share is a <button>. Android: Stars use selectable(role = Role.RadioButton) inside a selectableGroup() Row; the Share row is Role.Button.
- Name. Web: Stars aria-label "1 star" … "5 stars"; Share from its text. Android: Star icon contentDescription "1 star" … "5 stars"; Share reads "Share Feedback".
- Keyboard. Web: One Tab stop for the group (roving tabindex); arrow keys and Home / End move focus and the rating. Android: TalkBack: swipe through the stars (announced as a group), double-tap to rate.
- Touch target. Web: Stars use eq-touch at 48 px tall by the 40 px star pitch so neighbours don't overlap; Share's 48 px area sits in a 40 px row at the bottom of a clipped card, so about 44 px is tappable. Android: Each star sits in a 48 dp cell; the Share row is 48 dp high.
- Contrast. Web: Question text/primary 12.6:1. Empty stars (#2B2B2B @ 36%) are 2.1:1 on white (dark 2.9:1); filled stars are brand green #00B140, 2.85:1 (accepted brand decision; lime in dark 13.7:1). Share is text/action at 2.85:1 in light (accepted brand decision). Android: Same tokens, same ratios.
- State. Web: aria-checked on the chosen star; the filled vs outline shape also shows the rating. Android: selected on the chosen star; filled vs outline icon.
- Motion. Web: Star fill transition and press scale go to 0 ms under prefers-reduced-motion; hover previews the rating. Android: No animation.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Empty star outline rating/star-empty is 2.1:1 on white in light (2.9:1 in dark), below 3:1 for a control (FeedbackCard.tsx, Cards.kt).
- Accepted brand decision: filled stars and the Share Feedback label use brand green #00B140 on white (2.85:1) in light (FeedbackCard.tsx, Cards.kt).
- The Share Feedback row is 40 px high at the bottom of a card with overflow: hidden, so the TextButton's 48 px touch area is clipped to about 44 px (FeedbackCard.tsx).

Example: Interactive
```tsx
const [rating, setRating] = useState(0);

<FeedbackCard rating={rating} onRate={setRating} onShare={(r) => submit(r)} />
```
```kotlin
var rating by remember { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
FeedbackCard(
    question = "How would you rate the call?",
    rating = rating,
    onRatingChange = { rating = it },
    // Compose: the share callback takes no argument; read `rating` from state
    onShareFeedbackClick = {},
)
```

Example: Rated
```tsx
<FeedbackCard rating={4} />
```
```kotlin
// Compose: always controlled, so the question and rating callback are required
FeedbackCard(
    question = "How would you rate the call?",
    rating = 4,
    onRatingChange = {},
    onShareFeedbackClick = {},
)
```

#### Meet Your Assistant card (`meet-assistant-card`)

Introduces the voice assistant with its persona avatar and a “Call me” pill. Compact on Chats once the assistant is back; banner as a standalone promo.

- React: `import { MeetAssistantCard } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `MeetAssistantCard`
- Tokens: `gradient/meet-assistant`, `gradient/call-me`, `text/primary`, `text/action`, `text/secondary`, `text/on-action`, `text/placeholder`
- Source: Flows: Temporarily Unavailable

Do: Use the compact layout in the Chats promo slot, the same slot as What’s New. Keep “Call me” as the only action.

Don't: Don’t show it together with a What’s New card. Don’t crop or recolour the avatar-assistant art; the orb badge is part of the file.

Anatomy:
1. Card: Green-tint promo card in three layouts. (gradient/meet-assistant · compact radius lg (16), padding 14 16, gap 18 · banner radius xl (20), padding 20 16 20 18 (Compose 20 16 14 18), gap 12 · hero radius 2xl (24), padding 40 24 28, centred)
2. Assistant avatar: Persona art with the orb badge (decorative). (Asset avatar-assistant · compact 84 × 94 left · banner 100 × 112 bottom-right · hero 170 × 190 top)
3. Title: Meet Your Assistant. (compact Text subheading text/primary · banner Text title Bold text/action · hero Text headline Bold text/action, 28 above)
4. Body: Banner and hero only. (banner Text body1 text/secondary, 2 above · hero Text subheading Regular text/primary, 6 above)
5. CallMeButton: Starts a call with the assistant. (40 high with 48 touch area (52 full width in hero) · padding 0 22 0 18 · gap 8 · radius full · gradient/call-me · shadow 0 6 16 button/primary @28% · Icon call-sparkle 18 · Text button text/on-action)
6. Close: Optional dismiss. (web IconButton 32 with eq-touch, top 6 right 6 · Compose 48 dp box at the top-right corner · Icon close 20 · text/placeholder)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: The title is an <h3>; Call me and close are <button>s; the avatar art is decorative (alt=""). Android: Call me and close are clickable(role = Role.Button); the title is plain text; the avatar has contentDescription = null.
- Name. Web: Call me from its label (the icon is aria-hidden); close aria-label "Dismiss". Android: Call me reads its label; close icon contentDescription "Dismiss".
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to Call me, then Dismiss; Enter / Space activates. Android: TalkBack: swipe to the title, body, Call me and Dismiss.
- Touch target. Web: Call me (40 px) and close (32 px) use eq-touch for 48 px hit areas; the hero block is 52 px. Android: Call me uses touchTarget() for 48 dp (hero block 52 dp); close is a 48 dp box, offset 2 dp past the card's clipped corner, so about 46 dp is tappable.
- Contrast. Web: Compact title text/primary 12:1; banner body text/secondary 5.6:1; close icon text/placeholder 2.8:1 in light (3.6:1 dark). Banner and hero titles text/action on the tint are 2.6:1 and the Call me label white on brand green 2.85:1 in light (accepted brand decision); in dark lime titles are 11.9:1 and black on lime 17.4:1. Android: Same tokens, same ratios.
- State. Web: No state. Android: No state.
- Motion. Web: Static. Android: Static.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision: the Call me label is white on brand green (2.85:1) and the banner and hero titles are text/action on the tint (2.6:1) in light (SystemStatus.tsx, SystemStatus.kt).
- Close icon text/placeholder (black @ 40%) on gradient/meet-assistant is 2.8:1 in light, below 3:1 for an icon control (SystemStatus.tsx, SystemStatus.kt).
- Compose MeetAssistantCard titles have no semantics { heading() }, while web renders them as <h3> (SystemStatus.kt).
- Compose close box is offset 2 dp outside the card's clip, so its 48 dp touch area is cut to about 46 dp at the corner (SystemStatus.kt).

Example: Compact (Chats)
```tsx
<MeetAssistantCard onCall={startAssistantCall} onDismiss={dismiss} />
```
```kotlin
MeetAssistantCard(onCallClick = {}, onDismiss = {})
```

Example: Banner
```tsx
<MeetAssistantCard layout="banner" onCall={startAssistantCall} onDismiss={dismiss} />
```
```kotlin
MeetAssistantCard(layout = MeetAssistantLayout.Banner, onCallClick = {}, onDismiss = {})
```

#### System status card (`system-status-card`)

Takes the assistant toggle’s place on Chats while Equal AI is down: a SYSTEM STATUS pill, the sleeping robot, and a “Notify me when ready” pill that turns into a confirmation.

- React: `import { SystemStatusCard } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `SystemStatusCard`
- Tokens: `gradient/status-card`, `component/status-card/pill-bg`, `component/status-card/button`, `component/status-card/button-text`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/action`
- Source: Flows: Temporarily Unavailable

Do: Put it where the assistant toggle sits (HomeHeader `status`), so the outage reads as the assistant’s state. Hide promo cards (What’s New, Meet Your Assistant) while the card is showing.

Don't: Don’t show it for a single failed call; it means the whole service is down. Don’t keep the Notify pill tappable after the user has subscribed.

Anatomy:
1. Card: Warm gradient card in the assistant toggle's place. (min height 140 · radius xl (20) · padding 16 · gradient/status-card · overflow hidden)
2. Status pill: SYSTEM STATUS label. (20 high · padding 0 8 · radius full · status-card/pill-bg · Text overline at 10 · text/secondary)
3. Title: Temporarily Unavailable. (8 above · Text subheading at 18/24 Bold · text/primary · one line · heading)
4. Body: Short reassurance. (2 above · Text caption Regular · text/secondary · max width 190)
5. Notify pill: Subscribe to the recovery notice. (14 above · 32 high, 48 touch area · padding 0 14 0 12 · gap 6 · radius full · status-card/button · status-card/button-text · Icon notify-me 16 · Text buttonSmall Bold)
6. Confirmation: Replaces the pill after the tap. (Icon check 16 · gap 6 · Text buttonSmall Bold · text/action)
7. Sleeping mascot: Decorative art on the right. (Asset mascot-sleeping 104 · right 0 · vertically centred)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: The card is role="status" with an <h3> title; Notify is a <button>; the mascot is alt="". Android: The card has liveRegion = Polite; the title has semantics { heading() }; Notify is clickable(role = Role.Button); the mascot has no contentDescription.
- Name. Web: Notify from its text "Notify me when ready"; the icons are aria-hidden. Android: Notify reads its text; the icons are null.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to Notify; Enter / Space. When the confirmation replaces the button, focus moves to it (useFocusHandoff). Android: TalkBack: swipe to Notify, double-tap; the live region announces the confirmation.
- Touch target. Web: The 32 px Notify pill uses eq-touch for a 48 px hit area. Android: The 32 dp pill uses touchTarget() for a 48 dp touch area.
- Contrast. Web: Title text/primary 11.4:1 and body text/secondary 5.5:1 on the warmest stop; pill label #3D2600 on #FAAF39 7.6:1 (dark 8.3:1). The confirmation is text/action: brand green on the gradient is about 2.4–2.6:1 in light (accepted brand decision); lime in dark 11:1. Android: Same tokens, same ratios.
- State. Web: "notified" swaps the button for text with a check icon, so not colour alone; role=status announces it. Android: Same, announced through the polite live region.
- Motion. Web: Static. Android: Static.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision: the notified confirmation uses text/action #00B140 on gradient/status-card (about 2.4:1) in light (SystemStatus.tsx, SystemStatus.kt).

Example: Unavailable
```tsx
<SystemStatusCard onNotify={subscribeToRecovery} />
```
```kotlin
SystemStatusCard(state = SystemStatusState.Unavailable, onNotifyClick = {})
```

Example: Notify requested
```tsx
<SystemStatusCard state="notified" />
```
```kotlin
// The confirmation is not tappable, so onNotifyClick is never called in this state
SystemStatusCard(state = SystemStatusState.Notified, onNotifyClick = {})
```

Example: In the Chats header
```tsx
<HomeHeader assistantOn={on} status={down ? <SystemStatusCard state={notify} onNotify={subscribe} /> : undefined} />
```
```kotlin
var on by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }
var notify by remember { mutableStateOf(SystemStatusState.Unavailable) }
val down = true
HomeHeader(
    assistantOn = on,
    onAssistantChange = { on = it },
    status = if (down) {
        { SystemStatusCard(state = notify, onNotifyClick = { notify = SystemStatusState.Notified }) }
    } else {
        null
    },
)
```

#### What's New card (`whats-new-card`)

A dismissible announcement card with the NEW FEATURE badge, a heading, body copy and one CTA. Built in three layers: a flat fill, a blurred circle in the bottom-right corner, and the illustration on top of the circle.

- React: `import { WhatsNewCard } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `WhatsNewCard`
- Tokens: `whats-new/bg`, `whats-new/glow`, `text/action`, `text/secondary`, `text/placeholder`, `button/primary`
- Source: §22 What's New Card

Do: Keep the body to about two lines and one CTA that goes straight to the feature. Always offer onDismiss on the Chats list so the card can go away.

Don't: Don't stack more than one What's New card at a time. Don't add a second button; the card has a single commit.

Anatomy:
1. Card: Flat green-tint card with clipped layers. (width 322 (web; Compose fills) · min height 172 · radius xl (20) · whats-new/bg · padding 18 16 18 18 · text column stops 112 from the right)
2. Glow: Soft circle bottom-right, behind the art. (web: 150 circle, blur 32, right -36 bottom -48 · Compose: 230 dp radial gradient · whats-new/glow)
3. Illustration: Robot art on the right. (Asset whats-new-illustration 125 · right 4 · top 35 · decorative)
4. FeatureBadge: NEW FEATURE pill. (24 high · padding 0 10 0 8 · gap 6 · radius full · bg/surface · Emoji ⭐ 11 · Text badge uppercase text/secondary)
5. Heading: What the feature is. (12 above · Text title at 18/24 Bold · text/action)
6. Body: About two lines. (4 above · Text caption Regular · text/secondary · max 3 lines on Compose)
7. CTA: One filled button. (14 above · Button md 36 high, 48 touch area · leading Icon 18 (star) · button/primary · text/on-action)
8. Close: Optional dismiss. (web IconButton 32 with eq-touch, top 8 right 8 · Compose 48 dp box top-right · Icon close 22 · text/placeholder)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: The heading is an <h3>; CTA and close are <button>s; the illustration (alt="") and glow (aria-hidden) are decorative. Android: The heading has semantics { heading() }; the CTA is an EqualButton (Role.Button); close is a Role.Button box; the illustration has no contentDescription.
- Name. Web: CTA from its label; close aria-label "Dismiss"; the badge emoji is aria-hidden. Android: CTA from its label; close icon contentDescription "Close"; the badge emoji is hidden (EmojiGlyph).
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to the CTA, then Dismiss; Enter / Space activates. Android: TalkBack: swipe to the heading, body, CTA and Close; headings navigation finds the title.
- Touch target. Web: The 36 px CTA and the 32 px close both use eq-touch for a 48 px hit area. Android: The CTA uses minimumInteractiveComponentSize (48 dp); close is a 48 dp box.
- Contrast. Web: Body text/secondary 5.6:1 on whats-new/bg. The close icon text/placeholder is 2.8:1 in light (3.6:1 in dark). Heading text/action on #E5FFE7 is 2.7:1 and the CTA label white on #00B140 2.85:1 in light (accepted brand decision); in dark the lime heading is 11.9:1 and black on lime 17.4:1. Android: Same tokens, same ratios.
- State. Web: No state. Android: No state.
- Motion. Web: Static; the button press scale goes to 0 ms under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: Static.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision: the heading text/action #00B140 on whats-new/bg is 2.7:1 and the CTA label white on #00B140 is 2.85:1 in light (WhatsNewCard.tsx, Cards.kt, Button.css, Buttons.kt).
- Close icon text/placeholder (black @ 40%) on whats-new/bg is 2.8:1 in light, below 3:1 for an icon control (WhatsNewCard.tsx, Cards.kt).

Example: Default
```tsx
<WhatsNewCard width="100%" heading="Language Preference"
  body="Set your preferred language and choose how your assistant sounds"
  ctaLabel="Try Voices" ctaIcon="translate" onCta={openVoices} onDismiss={dismiss} />
```
```kotlin
WhatsNewCard(
    title = "Language Preference",
    body = "Set your preferred language and choose how your assistant sounds",
    buttonLabel = "Try Voices",
    buttonIcon = EqualIcons.Translate,
    onButtonClick = {},
    onCloseClick = {},
)
```

Example: Custom badge and icon, not dismissible
```tsx
<WhatsNewCard width="100%" badge="Just added" heading="Instructions"
  body="Tell your assistant how to handle deliveries, sales calls and more."
  ctaLabel="Add instruction" ctaIcon="add" />
```

```kotlin
    badgeText = "Just added",
    title = "Instructions",

    buttonLabel = "Add instruction",
```

### Group: Chat

#### AI panel (`ai-panel`)

The assistant's bottom panel inside a conversation: a suggestion from the orb, large action chips and a composer; AiSuggestion is the avatar-plus-prompt line on its own.

- React: `import { AiChatPanel, AiSuggestion } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `AiChatPanel`, `AiSuggestion`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `text/secondary`, `text/primary`, `gradient/chip-large`, `action/stroke/unread`
- Source: §12b AI Chat — Within other conversation · §16 AI Suggestion

Do: Phrase the prompt as a question the user can answer with one chip ("Want me to send Amit a quick reply on WhatsApp?"). Offer at most two or three emoji chips, the most likely one first. Hide the composer (composer={false}) when only a quick decision makes sense, like during a live call.

Don't: Don't put a filled Button in the panel; the actions are large chips. Don't write the prompt in green; the assistant's words are text/secondary here.

Anatomy:
1. Panel: Bottom sheet-like panel with rounded top corners. (bg/surface · radius 2xl (24) 24 0 0 · padding 20 16 16 · shadow 0 -4 16 (web))
2. Suggestion: Equal orb and the assistant's prompt. (AiAvatar 36 · gap 12 · Text body1 text/secondary)
3. Action chips: Horizontally scrolling row of large emoji chips. (margin-top 20 (web) / 24 (Compose) · gap 6 · LargeActionChip 40 high, 48 touch area · padding 0 12 0 10 · radius full · gradient/chip-large · 1 px action/stroke/unread · Emoji 14 · Text button text/primary)
4. Composer: Message input with the send button. (margin-top 16 (web) / 20 (Compose) · input 45 high, radius full, padding 0 20, bg/surface, 1 px stroke/subtle · placeholder text/secondary · send 45 circle gradient/fab (gradient/send-disabled when empty))
5. AiSuggestion: Avatar plus prompt on its own. (AiAvatar 36 · gap 12 · Text body1 · 7 top · tone primary or secondary (web), text/primary (Compose))

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: The panel is a <section>; chips are <button>s; the composer is a <form> with an <input> and a submit <button>. Android: Column; chips are clickable(role = Role.Button); VoiceInputBar is a BasicTextField plus a Role.Button send.
- Name. Web: Orb role=img "Equal AI"; chips from their label (the emoji is aria-hidden); input aria-label "Message"; send aria-label "Send". Android: AiAvatar "Equal AI"; chips read their label (EmojiGlyph is hidden); the field has contentDescription "Message"; send reads "Send".
- Keyboard. Web: Tab through chips, input and send; Enter submits; send is disabled while the input is empty. Android: TalkBack: swipe to chips, field and send; the IME Send action submits when there is text.
- Touch target. Web: Chips and send use eq-touch for a 48 px hit area, but the chip row scrolls (overflow-x: auto), which clips the chip area to about 46 px high. Android: Chips use minimumInteractiveComponentSize (48 dp); send uses touchTarget() for 48 dp around the 45 dp circle.
- Contrast. Web: Prompt text/secondary 5.7:1 on white; chip label text/primary 12.2:1 on the lime-washed fill; placeholder text/secondary 5.7:1. The chip border (green @ 36%) is 1.5:1, but the label marks the control. Android: Same tokens, same ratios.
- State. Web: Send uses the native disabled attribute while empty; the focused input gets only the solid 1.5 px stroke/focus outline (no black ring). Android: Send is clickable(enabled = false) while empty; disabled chips draw at 45% and are exposed as disabled.
- Motion. Web: eq-pressable press scale and composer border / shadow transitions go to 0 ms under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: Press feedback only.

Known accessibility gaps:
- LargeActionChip's 48 px eq-touch area is clipped by the scrolling ChipRow (overflow-x: auto with 2 / 4 px padding), so chips in AiChatPanel are about 46 px tall to touch (ActionChip.tsx).

Example: After a call
```tsx
<AiChatPanel
  prompt="Want me to send Amit a quick reply on WhatsApp?"
  actions={[
    { label: 'Reply on WhatsApp', emoji: '💬' },
    { label: 'Add to Calendar', emoji: '🗓️' },
  ]}
  composer={{ onSend: send }} />
```
```kotlin
var draft by remember { mutableStateOf("") }

AiChatPanel(
    prompt = "Want me to send Amit a quick reply on WhatsApp?",
    actions = listOf(
        ActionChipData("Reply on WhatsApp", "💬"),
        ActionChipData("Add to Calendar", "🗓️"),
    ),
    onActionClick = {},
    composerValue = draft,
    onComposerValueChange = { draft = it },
    onSend = {},
)
```

Example: During a live call, no composer
```tsx
<AiChatPanel
  prompt="Arnav is at the gate with a parcel. Want to take over?"
  actions={[
    { label: 'Takeover', emoji: '📞' },
    { label: 'Ask to reschedule', emoji: '🗓️' },
  ]}
  composer={false} />
```
```kotlin
var draft by remember { mutableStateOf("") }

// Compose: AiChatPanel always shows the composer; there is no composer = false.
AiChatPanel(
    prompt = "Arnav is at the gate with a parcel. Want to take over?",
    actions = listOf(
        ActionChipData("Takeover", "📞"),
        ActionChipData("Ask to reschedule", "🗓️"),
    ),
    onActionClick = {},
    composerValue = draft,
    onComposerValueChange = { draft = it },
    onSend = {},
)
```

Example: AI suggestion
```tsx
<AiSuggestion>Want me to send Amit a quick reply on WhatsApp?</AiSuggestion>
<AiSuggestion tone="secondary">I can also add Sunday dinner to your calendar.</AiSuggestion>
```
```kotlin
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(16.dp)) {
    AiSuggestion("Want me to send Amit a quick reply on WhatsApp?")
    // Compose: no `tone`; AiSuggestion is always text/primary.
    AiSuggestion("I can also add Sunday dinner to your calendar.")
}
```

#### Call controls (`call-controls`)

The in-call parts of the VoIP "Call me" screen (vOIP design): the 52 control buttons (speaker and mute are independent switches, end is the rose pill), the running timer, the assistant avatar with its ripples, and the status line.

- React: `import { CallControlBar, CallTimer, CallAvatar, CallStatusLine } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `CallControlButton`, `CallControlBar`, `CallTimer`, `CallAvatar`, `CallStatusLine`, `CallScreen`
- Tokens: `call-control/bg`, `call-control/active-bg`, `call-control/active-icon`, `button/end-call`, `text/on-end-call`, `gradient/assistant-call`
- Source: vOIP · Call screen (Connecting / Connected / Call ended)

Props of `CallTimer`:
- `seconds`: `number`. Elapsed seconds, shown as m:ss (h:mm:ss past an hour). Use useCallTimer to run it.

Props of `CallStatusLine`:
- `phase`: `'connecting' | 'calling' | 'ringing' | 'connected' | 'ended'`. Phase text, announced politely.
- `muted?`: `boolean`. Connected and muted: "On mute" with the mic-off icon.

Do: Keep speaker and mute as separate switches: each says its own state. Ask for the microphone at the moment the user taps Call me, never earlier.

Don't: Don't use the rose end-call colour for anything but ending a call. Don't hide the timer once connected; it is how the user knows the line is live.

Anatomy:
1. Avatar: Who the call is with. (200 disc gradient/assistant-call with the assistant bust or initials · ripple rings 280 / 360 / 440)
2. Status line: Connecting, Calling, Ringing, Connected or Call ended. (title · text/secondary · "On mute" with mic-off when muted)
3. Timer: Elapsed time once connected. (body2 tabular figures · m:ss)
4. Control bar: Speaker, mute and end. (52 circles call-control/bg · active call-control/active-bg + active-icon · end pill button/end-call with text/on-end-call icon · gap 24)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Speaker and mute are role='switch' with aria-checked; end is a button; the bar is role='group' named "Call controls". Android: Speaker and mute use toggleable(role = Role.Switch); end is Role.Button.
- Name. Web: "Speaker", "Mute", "End call" (icon-only, so aria-label). Android: contentDescription on each control.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab through speaker, mute, end; Space / Enter activates. Android: D-pad focus in the same order.
- Touch target. Web: 52 circles, above 44. Android: 52dp, above 48.
- Contrast. Web: Icons on call-control/bg meet 3:1; the end icon on rose meets 4.5:1. Android: Same tokens.
- State. Web: aria-checked plus the active fill; the mute icon changes to mic-off. Android: Toggle state plus a glyph change.
- Motion. Web: Ripples and pulse stop under reduced motion. Android: rememberReduceMotion() stops the ripples.

Known accessibility gaps:
- The status line is role='status' on web; on Android the status text has no liveRegion yet, so phase changes aren't announced.

Example: Control bar
```tsx
const [speaker, setSpeaker] = useState(false);
const [muted, setMuted] = useState(false);

<CallControlBar
  speaker={speaker}
  muted={muted}
  onSpeaker={() => setSpeaker((v) => !v)}
  onMute={() => setMuted((v) => !v)}
  onEnd={endCall}
/>
```
```kotlin
var speaker by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
var muted by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
CallControlBar(
    speaker = speaker,
    muted = muted,
    onSpeaker = { speaker = !speaker },
    onMute = { muted = !muted },
    onEnd = { /* end the call */ },
)
```

Example: Avatar, status and timer
```tsx
<CallAvatar ripples size={160} />
<CallStatusLine phase="connected" />
<CallTimer seconds={83} />
```
```kotlin
CallAvatar(ripples = true, size = 160.dp)
CallStatusLine(phase = CallPhase.Connected)
CallTimer(seconds = 83)
```

#### Call status (`call-status`)

Centred thread markers: the day divider, call start/end events, and a notice when the thread switches to the assistant.

- React: `import { DayDivider, ThreadEvent, ThreadNotice } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `DayDivider`, `ThreadEvent`, `ThreadNotice`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `stroke/subtle`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `notice/bg`
- Source: §21 Call Status Indicators

Props of `DayDivider`:
- `label`: `string`. "Today", "12 July".

Props of `ThreadEvent`:
- `label`: `string`. "Call Started 03:31", "Call Ended 03:31".

Props of `ThreadNotice`:
- `children`: `ReactNode`. Notice text (captionWrap, centred, max width 240).

Do: Bracket every call with Call Started / Call Ended events. Use a ThreadNotice when the conversation changes hands ("You are now talking to your AI assistant").

Don't: Don't use a ThreadNotice for ordinary messages; it is for system state changes only. Don't style these as bubbles; they are centred pills without avatars.

Anatomy:
1. DayDivider: Centred pill naming the day. (24 high (web) / 22 dp (Compose) · padding 0 14 · radius sm (8) · bg/surface · 1 px stroke/subtle · Text micro text/primary)
2. ThreadEvent: Same pill for call start and end. (same pill · Text micro text/secondary)
3. ThreadNotice: Centred note when the thread changes hands. (max width 240 (web) / 232 dp (Compose) · padding 8 16 · radius sm (8) · notice/bg · Text captionWrap text/secondary centred)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Plain divs and spans with text (the notice is a <p>); no separator or status role. Inside MessageList they sit in its role="log". Android: Plain Box + EqualText; no extra semantics.
- Name. Web: Read as their visible text ("Today", "Call Started 03:31"). Android: Read as their visible text.
- Keyboard. Web: Not focusable; read in order when browsing. Android: TalkBack: swipe to each as plain text.
- Touch target. Web: Not interactive. Android: Not interactive.
- Contrast. Web: DayDivider text/primary 12.6:1 on white; ThreadEvent text/secondary 5.7:1; notice text/secondary 5.7:1 on notice/bg (dark 6.4:1). Android: Same tokens, same ratios.
- State. Web: No state. Android: No state.
- Motion. Web: No animation. Android: No animation.

Example: All indicators
```tsx
<MessageList>
  <DayDivider label="Today" />
  <ThreadEvent label="Call Started 03:31" />
  <ThreadEvent label="Call Ended 03:31" />
  <ThreadNotice>Call has ended. You are now talking to your AI assistant.</ThreadNotice>
</MessageList>
```
```kotlin
Column(
    Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally,
    verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp),
) {
    DayDivider("Today")
    ThreadEvent("Call Started 03:31")
    ThreadEvent("Call Ended 03:31")
    ThreadNotice("Call has ended. You are now talking to your AI assistant.")
}
```

Example: In a thread
```tsx
<ChatWallpaper>
  <MessageList>
    <DayDivider label="12 July" />
    <ThreadEvent label="Call Started 18:02" />
    <ChatBubble kind="outgoing" sender="Equal AI" time="18:02">Hi, who is this?</ChatBubble>
    …
    <ThreadEvent label="Call Ended 18:04" />
    <ThreadNotice>Call has ended. You are now talking to your AI assistant.</ThreadNotice>
  </MessageList>
</ChatWallpaper>
```
```kotlin
ChatWallpaper {
    Column(
        Modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(vertical = 16.dp),
        horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally,
        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp),
    ) {
        DayDivider("12 July")
        ThreadEvent("Call Started 18:02")
        ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Outgoing, sender = "Equal AI", timestamp = "18:02", message = "Hi, who is this?")
        ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Incoming, incomingCategory = EqualCategory.NA, sender = "Amit Nanda",
            timestamp = "18:02", message = "It's Amit. Dinner at mine this Sunday, 8 PM?")
        ThreadEvent("Call Ended 18:04")
        ThreadNotice("Call has ended. You are now talking to your AI assistant.")
    }
}
```

#### Call summary (`call-summary`)

The post-call card in a thread: a recording player with a coded waveform and speed pill, the assistant's summary, and an optional share footer or "2 instructions applied in this call" tag.

- React: `import { CallSummary, VoicePlayer } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `CallSummaryBubble`, `VoiceNotePlayer`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `voice/player-bg`, `voice/player-stroke`, `stroke/subtle`, `waveform/bar`, `waveform/bar-played`, `playback/pill-bg`, `text/on-dark`, `text/secondary`, `text/primary`, `text/action`
- Source: §11 Chat Bubbles · Voice note + Call Summary bubble

Do: Write the summary as the outcome for the user ("Amit invited you to dinner… confirm by tonight"), not a transcript. Tag the card 🪄 "2 instructions applied in this call" when one of the user's instructions handled the call. Keep the same `seed` for a recording so its waveform is stable.

Don't: Don't use an image for the waveform; it is coded. Don't show the player for calls without a recording; use `noRecording`.

Anatomy:
1. Card: White card that holds the recording, the summary and the footer. (width 268 (Compose Dp.Unspecified fills) · bg/surface · radius lg (16) · overflow hidden / clip)
2. Voice player: Recording box with play, waveform, speed pill and times. (8 margin · voice/player-bg (sent: voice/player-bg-sent) · radius md (12) · padding 10 / 10 / 6 (web), 10 (Compose) · 1 px voice/player-stroke, button/primary while playing)
3. Play / pause: Toggles playback. (Icon play / pause 22 · text/secondary · 48 touch area · gap 8)
4. VoiceWaveform: Coded bars that fill as the recording plays. (web: 28 bars, 3 wide, gap 2, 24 high · Compose EqualWaveform: 2 wide, gap 2, 22 high · waveform/bar · waveform/bar-played)
5. Speed pill: Cycles 1x → 1.2x → 1.5x → 2x. (22 high · min width 34 (web) · padding 0 8 · radius full · playback/pill-bg · Text caption tabular · text/on-dark (sent: bg/surface + text/primary) · 48 touch area)
6. Times: Elapsed and total under the two ends of the waveform. (Text micro · text/secondary · 4 above)
7. Label and summary: "Call Summary" caption over the summary text. (Text caption text/secondary · Text body1 text/primary · padding 0 10 6 (web) / 0 8 8 (Compose))
8. Tag and time: Optional line under the summary saying which instructions ran (🪄 2 instructions applied in this call), then the timestamp on the right. (8 above · padding 4 · Emoji 12 + 12 Regular text/secondary · time Text micro text/secondary, right-aligned)
9. Share footer: Divider and a centred Share action. (divider stroke/subtle · row 44 (web, TextButton with 48 touch area) / 48 (Compose) · share icon 18 · button text/action)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Play and speed are native <button>s; the waveform is role="progressbar"; Share is a <button>. Android: Play and speed are clickable(role = Role.Button); the waveform carries progressBarRangeInfo; the Share row is Role.Button.
- Name. Web: Play aria-label switches "Play" / "Pause"; speed aria-label "Playback speed 1x"; waveform "Playback position" with aria-valuetext "00:12 of 02:37"; Share from its text. The tag emoji is aria-hidden. Android: Play icon contentDescription "Play" / "Pause"; speed reads its label ("1x") with onClickLabel "Change speed"; waveform "Playback" with stateDescription "0:12 of 0:30"; Share reads "Share". The tag emoji is hidden (EmojiGlyph).
- Keyboard. Web: Tab reaches play, speed and Share; Enter/Space activates. No seek control. Android: TalkBack: swipe to play, waveform, speed, Share; double-tap to activate.
- Touch target. Web: Play, speed and Share use eq-touch for a 48 px hit area around the smaller visuals. Android: Play and speed use touchTarget() for a 48 dp touch and TalkBack area around the 22 dp visuals; the Share row is 48 dp high.
- Contrast. Web: Summary text/primary 12.6:1; label, times and tag text/secondary 5.7:1; speed white on #5E5E5E 6.5:1. Unplayed bars #D9D9D9 are 1.4:1 and played bars green 2.85:1, but the elapsed time text carries the same progress. Share is text/action: brand green #00B140 on white is 2.85:1 (accepted brand decision); lime in dark is 13.7:1. Android: Same tokens, same ratios.
- State. Web: Play/pause is told by the label; progress by aria-valuenow / valuetext and the elapsed time. Locked audio blurs the player (aria-hidden) under an Unlock Audio pill; locked="all" also reads the locked sentence for the summary. Android: Same; the locked player uses clearAndSetSemantics {} under UnlockAudioPill, and CallSummaryLock.All wraps the summary in LockedContent.
- Motion. Web: Stroke and bar colour transitions (duration-fast) drop to 0 ms under prefers-reduced-motion via base.css; playback progress itself is functional. Android: Colour changes are instant; waveform progress is driven by the caller.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision: the Share action uses text/action #00B140 on white (2.85:1), below 4.5:1 in light (VoiceNote.tsx, VoiceNote.kt).
- With locked set, the blurred VoicePlayer is only aria-hidden with pointer-events: none, so its Play and speed buttons stay in the Tab order as hidden focus stops; it should be inert (VoiceNote.tsx).
- With locked set, CallSummaryBubble lays a matchParentSize clickable over the blurred player with no role or label, so TalkBack lands on an unnamed button next to Unlock Audio (VoiceNote.kt).

Example: With recording and share
```tsx
<CallSummary
  summary="Amit invited you to dinner this Sunday, 8 PM at his place. He asked you to confirm by tonight."
  time="03:21" onShare={share} />
```
```kotlin
var playing by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
var speed by remember { mutableStateOf(PlaybackSpeed.X1) }

CallSummaryBubble(
    summary = "Amit invited you to dinner this Sunday, 8 PM at his place. He asked you to confirm by tonight.",
    timestamp = "03:21",
    voiceNote = {
        // Compose: the player is controlled; drive progress/elapsed from your media player.
        VoiceNotePlayer(isPlaying = playing, onPlayPauseClick = { playing = !playing },
            progress = 0f, elapsed = "0:00", total = "2:37",
            speed = speed, onSpeedChange = { speed = it })
    },
    onShareClick = {},
)
```

Example: Instruction applied
```tsx
<CallSummary
  summary="Priya from Dr. Mehta's clinic confirmed your appointment for tomorrow at 10 AM. Bring your previous reports."
  time="03:32" tag={{ emoji: '🪄', label: '2 instructions applied in this call' }} />
```
```kotlin
CallSummaryBubble(
    summary = "Priya from Dr. Mehta's clinic confirmed your appointment for tomorrow at 10 AM. Bring your previous reports.",
    timestamp = "03:32",
    tag = CallSummaryTag(label = "2 instructions applied in this call", emoji = "🪄"),
    modifier = Modifier.width(264.dp),
)
```

Example: Summary only
```tsx
<CallSummary noRecording
  summary="Vijay from NoBroker called with an offer on a 2BHK flat in Sector 12. You said you were not interested and ended the call."
  time="03:21" />
```
```kotlin
// No voiceNote slot = no recording player.
CallSummaryBubble(
    summary = "Vijay from NoBroker called with an offer on a 2BHK flat in Sector 12. You said you were not interested and ended the call.",
    timestamp = "03:21",
)
```

Example: Voice player
```tsx
<VoicePlayer duration={94} seed={7} />
```
```kotlin
var playing by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
var speed by remember { mutableStateOf(PlaybackSpeed.X1) }

// Compose: no `seed`; pass `samples` for a recording-specific waveform (defaults are fixed).
VoiceNotePlayer(
    isPlaying = playing,
    onPlayPauseClick = { playing = !playing },
    progress = 0f,
    elapsed = "0:00",
    total = "1:34",
    speed = speed,
    onSpeedChange = { speed = it },
)
```

#### Chat bubble (`chat-bubble`)

Message bubbles for a call thread: outgoing (Equal AI or you on the call), incoming (the caller) and assistant (Equal AI talking to you), stacked with MessageList.

- React: `import { ChatBubble, MessageList } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `ChatBubble`
- Tokens: `chat-bubble/user-bg`, `chat-bubble/user-title`, `chat-bubble/other-bg`, `chat-bubble/contact-title`, `bg/surface`, `text/action`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`
- Source: §11 Chat Bubbles

Do: Use `outgoing` with sender "Equal AI" when the assistant speaks for the user on a call, and "You" after a takeover. Use `assistant` only when Equal AI is talking to the user, not to the caller. Set first={false} on consecutive bubbles from the same sender.

Don't: Don't mix up outgoing and assistant; the green byline means Equal AI is addressing you. Don't put custom cards inside a padded bubble; use `bare`.

Anatomy:
1. Avatar: Caller category art (incoming) or the Equal orb (assistant), shown on the first bubble of a group only. (CategoryAvatar 28 dp · AiAvatar 24 dp · 28 dp column (web) / 28 or 24 dp spacer on follow-ups (Compose) · gap 8 · outgoing has none)
2. Bubble container: Rounded fill whose colour and side tell outgoing, incoming and assistant apart. (max width 264 · min width 72 (web) · radius md (12) · padding 8 / 10 / 6 · chat-bubble/user-bg · chat-bubble/other-bg · bg/surface)
3. Corners: The first bubble of a group squares its top-outer corner; follow-ups round all four. (radius 12 · first: top-left 0 (incoming, assistant) or top-right 0 (outgoing) · first={false} / isFirstInGroup = false: 12 on all four · no notch)
4. Sender line: Who is speaking, on the first bubble of a group. (Text body2 · chat-bubble/user-title (outgoing) · chat-bubble/contact-title (incoming) · text/action (assistant) · one line on Compose)
5. Attachment: Optional content such as a voice note, between the sender and the message (Compose). (Compose attachment slot · 2 dp above, 4 dp below (plus the 2 dp column gap))
6. Message: The message text, or custom content with bare; locked blurs it under the crown-lock badge. (Text body1 · text/primary · bare removes padding, sender and time (web) · locked wraps it in Locked / LockedContent)
7. Timestamp: Time of the message: beside a one-line message, on its own row under a longer one. (Text micro · text/secondary · one line: same row, gap 8, 4 dp below the text line · more than one line: own row, right-aligned, 2 dp above)
8. MessageList: Vertical list that applies the group rhythm (web; on Compose the caller stacks bubbles). (role=log · gap 4 · 8 dp extra before a new group · padding 12)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: MessageList is role="log" with aria-label "Messages", so new bubbles are announced politely. Bubbles are plain divs; the orb and category avatar are images. Android: Each bubble row uses semantics(mergeDescendants = true), so sender, message and time are one TalkBack stop; controls inside an attachment stay separate.
- Name. Web: Read as text: avatar name ("Equal AI" or the category label), sender, message, time. Follow-ups and bare bubbles get a visually hidden "Sender: " prefix (assistant defaults to "Equal AI"). Android: Avatars are decorative (contentDescription = null). Follow-ups add the hidden sender back as the row's contentDescription; the message and time are read as written.
- Keyboard. Web: Not interactive; screen readers reach it in reading order. Android: Not interactive; TalkBack swipes one bubble at a time.
- Touch target. Web: Nothing to tap in the bubble itself; controls in custom (bare) content bring their own targets. Android: Nothing to tap in the bubble itself; an attachment (VoiceNotePlayer) brings its own 48 dp targets.
- Contrast. Web: Message text/primary 12.2:1 on user-bg and 12.6:1 on white; time text/secondary 5.7:1; incoming sender #AF6307 4.55:1; outgoing sender #006223 7.2:1. The assistant sender is text/action: brand green #00B140 on white is 2.85:1 (accepted brand decision); lime in dark is 13.7:1. Android: Same tokens through EqualTheme.colors, same ratios.
- State. Web: Side and fill show who sent it; the hidden sender prefix keeps follow-ups attributable. Locked bubbles hide the text and read "Locked. Unlock Equal Unlimited to see this." Android: Same; LockedContent uses clearAndSetSemantics with the same locked sentence.
- Motion. Web: No animation. Android: No animation.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision: the assistant sender line uses text/action #00B140 on bg/surface (2.85:1), below 4.5:1 in light (ChatBubble.tsx, ChatBubble.kt).
- The web avatar is announced ("Equal AI" orb, category name) right before a sender line that says the same thing, so screen readers hear the name twice; Compose already passes contentDescription = null (ChatBubble.tsx).
- Compose has no MessageList equivalent with liveRegion, so a live call thread does not announce new bubbles the way the web role="log" does (ChatBubble.kt).

Example: A call thread
```tsx
<MessageList>
  <ChatBubble kind="outgoing" sender="Equal AI" time="03:21">Hi, who is this?</ChatBubble>
  <ChatBubble kind="incoming" sender="Dr Mehta Clinic" time="03:21">
    This is Priya from Dr. Mehta's clinic. Your appointment is confirmed for tomorrow.
  </ChatBubble>
  <ChatBubble kind="outgoing" sender="You" time="03:21">Yes, I'll be there at 10 AM</ChatBubble>
  <ChatBubble kind="assistant" sender="Equal AI" time="03:21">
    Hey Keshav! Here is the summary of your call
  </ChatBubble>
</MessageList>
```
```kotlin
// Compose: no MessageList; a Column with 12dp spacing gives the between-group rhythm.
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)) {
    ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Outgoing, sender = "Equal AI", timestamp = "03:21", message = "Hi, who is this?")
    ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Incoming, sender = "Dr Mehta Clinic", timestamp = "03:21",
        message = "This is Priya from Dr. Mehta's clinic. Your appointment is confirmed for tomorrow.")
    ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Outgoing, sender = "You", timestamp = "03:21", message = "Yes, I'll be there at 10 AM")
    ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Incoming, sender = "Dr Mehta Clinic", timestamp = "03:21",
        message = "Great. Please bring your previous reports too.")
    ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Assistant, sender = "Equal AI", timestamp = "03:21",
        message = "Hey Keshav! Here is the summary of your call")
}
```

Example: Corners and grouping
```tsx
<ChatBubble kind="incoming" category="real-estate" sender="Vijay · NoBroker" time="03:21">
  I have an offer on a 2BHK flat in Sector 12.
</ChatBubble>
<ChatBubble kind="incoming" category="real-estate" first={false} time="03:21">
  Are you free for a site visit this weekend?
</ChatBubble>
<ChatBubble kind="outgoing" sender="Equal AI" time="03:22">
  Thanks, but Keshav is not interested right now.
</ChatBubble>
```
```kotlin
Column {
    ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Incoming, incomingCategory = EqualCategory.RealEstate,
        sender = "Vijay · NoBroker", timestamp = "03:21",
        message = "I have an offer on a 2BHK flat in Sector 12.")
    // Follow-up in the same group: 4dp gap, no avatar, no sender line.
    ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Incoming, incomingCategory = EqualCategory.RealEstate,
        isFirstInGroup = false, timestamp = "03:21", modifier = Modifier.padding(top = 4.dp),
        message = "Are you free for a site visit this weekend?")
    ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Outgoing, sender = "Equal AI", timestamp = "03:22",
        modifier = Modifier.padding(top = 12.dp), message = "Thanks, but Keshav is not interested right now.")
}
```

Example: Bare content
```tsx
<ChatBubble kind="assistant" bare>
  <CallSummary noRecording summary="Delivery agent will arrive between 4 and 5 PM." time="03:21" />
</ChatBubble>
```
```kotlin
// Compose: ChatBubble has no `bare` mode; lay the AI avatar beside the card yourself.
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
    AiAvatar(size = AiAvatarSize.Small)
    CallSummaryBubble(
        summary = "Delivery agent will arrive between 4 and 5 PM.",
        timestamp = "03:21",
        modifier = Modifier.width(240.dp),
    )
}
```

#### Chat list item (`chat-list-item`)

A row in the Chats list with avatar, name, date, preview, unread count and the small action chips; states come from `unread` and `selected`.

- React: `import { ChatListItem } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `ChatListItem`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `action-card/highlight`, `state/chat-pressed`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/action`, `button/primary`, `text/on-action`
- Source: §6 Chat List Item

Do: Give unknown callers their category art and saved contacts their initials. Offer the next step as chips on the row (📞 Call Back, 🗓️ Add to Calendar) so it is one tap from the list. Use long-press to enter selection mode.

Don't: Don't set chip states yourself; the row derives them from unread and selected. Don't let the preview wrap; it is one line with an ellipsis.

Anatomy:
1. Row container: Full-width tappable row; fills green when selected. (padding 12 v / 16 start (web 0 end, Compose 16) · bg/surface · selected action-card/highlight · pressed state/chat-pressed · gap 16 · web focus 2px text/action inset outline)
2. Avatar: Contact avatar or the orb for Equal AI. (48 · selected shows the check badge)
3. Name: Contact name, one line, with a verified tick for the official chat. (Text atom · subheading 16/500 text/primary · verified 16 text/action, label 'Verified' · gap 4)
4. Date: Time or date of the last message. (micro 12/500 tabular · text/action when unread (web also when selected), else text/secondary · gap 8)
5. Preview: Last message or summary, blurred when locked. (body1 14/400 text/secondary · one line · locked blur 4 + crown-lock 16)
6. Unread count: CountBadge at the end of the preview line; the crown-lock replaces it when locked. (20 · button/primary · gap 8)
7. Action chips: Scrolling row of SmallActionChips; state follows the row. (margin-top 8 · gap 12 · unread / read / outlined · gold crown-locked with lockedActions)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: A <div role='button' tabIndex=0> with aria-pressed when `selected` is set, containing the chip <button>s. Android: combinedClickable(role = Role.Button) on the Row; chips are separate Role.Button nodes.
- Name. Web: All row text in order: category or orb name, name, 'Verified', date, preview, 'N unread'; locked previews read 'Locked. Unlock Equal Unlimited to see this.' Android: Merged text of the row; LockedContent replaces the preview with the same locked message.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to the row, Enter or Space opens it; long-press maps to the context-menu event (right-click or the Menu key). Chips are later Tab stops. Focus draws a 2px text/action inset outline. Android: TalkBack: double-tap opens, double-tap-and-hold triggers onLongClick, announced as 'Select'. No visible hardware-keyboard focus.
- Touch target. Web: Row is at least 72px high and full width; chips use .eq-touch. Android: Row is full width and at least 72dp; chips get 48dp.
- Contrast. Web: Name 12.6:1, preview and read date text/secondary 5.7:1; unread date text/action #00B140 is 2.85:1 in light (lime in dark passes). Android: Same tokens as web.
- State. Web: Unread shows the count badge as well as a green date; selected sets aria-pressed plus the avatar check ('Selected') and highlight fill. Android: Unread shows the count badge; selected is set in semantics and drawn (fill, check 'Selected').
- Motion. Web: Background fades over 200ms; zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: No ripple or animation; the pressed wash is instant.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision: ChatListItem.tsx / ChatListItem.kt unread date in text/action #00B140 on white is 2.85:1 for 12sp text in light mode, and the web focus outline in the same green is below 3:1.
- ChatListItem.tsx: role='button' wraps the chip <button>s, which nests interactive controls; the row should be a list item with a separate open button or link.
- ChatListItem.kt: combinedClickable uses indication = null, so hardware-keyboard focus on the row is invisible.

Example: Unread and read
```tsx
<ChatListItem name="Arnav Raj" preview="You have a visitor" date="Yesterday"
  unread={5} avatar={{ category: 'na' }}
  actions={[
    { label: 'Call Back', emoji: '📞' },
    { label: 'Update Address', emoji: '✏️' },
    { label: 'Add to Calendar', emoji: '🗓️' },
  ]} />
<ChatListItem name="Amit Nanda" preview="Count me in for Sunday 8 PM 👍" date="12 July"
  avatar={{ initials: 'AN' }} actions={[{ label: 'Call Back', emoji: '📞' }]} />
```
```kotlin
ChatListItem(
    name = "Arnav Raj",
    preview = "You have a visitor",
    date = "Yesterday",
    state = ChatListItemState.Unread,
    unreadCount = 5,
    category = EqualCategory.NA,
    chips = listOf(
        ActionChipData("Call Back", "📞"),
        ActionChipData("Update Address", "✏️"),
        ActionChipData("Add to Calendar", "🗓️"),
    ),
)
ChatListItem(
    name = "Amit Nanda",
    preview = "Count me in for Sunday 8 PM 👍",
    date = "12 July",
    initials = "AN",
    chips = listOf(ActionChipData("Call Back", "📞")),
)
```

Example: Long-press to select
```tsx
<ChatListItem name="Dr Mehta Clinic" preview="Appointment confirmed for tomorrow, 10 AM"
  date="03:21" unread={2} avatar={{ category: 'others' }}
  actions={[{ label: 'Add to Calendar', emoji: '🗓️' }, { label: 'Call Back', emoji: '📞' }]}
  selected={selected} onLongPress={() => setSelected(true)} />
```
```kotlin
var selected by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }

ChatListItem(
    name = "Dr Mehta Clinic",
    preview = "Appointment confirmed for tomorrow, 10 AM",
    date = "03:21",

    unreadCount = 2,

    chips = listOf(ActionChipData("Add to Calendar", "🗓️"), ActionChipData("Call Back", "📞")),
    onLongClick = { selected = true },
    onClick = { selected = false },
)
```

```kotlin
        initials = "AN", chips = callBack)

        category = EqualCategory.RealEstate, chips = callBack)
```

#### Chat wallpaper (`chat-wallpaper`)

The doodle pattern behind chat threads and the instruction setup chat, tinted by token so one tile serves light and dark.

- React: `import { ChatWallpaper } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `ChatWallpaper`
- Tokens: `chat/wallpaper-bg`, `chat/wallpaper-pattern`
- Source: Flows · Chat wallpaper

Do: Use it behind chat threads and the "Setting up instruction" chat only. Give it minHeight: 100% so the pattern fills short threads.

Don't: Don't put the wallpaper behind lists or settings screens. Don't tint the pattern yourself; it reads chat/wallpaper-pattern in both themes.

Anatomy:
1. Background: Flat fill behind the thread. (chat/wallpaper-bg (#F5F5F6 / #141414))
2. Doodle pattern: Tiled doodles masked and tinted by token. (360 × 750 tile · chat/wallpaper-pattern rgba(115,115,115,0.08) · web ::before mask, z-index -1, pointer-events none · Compose drawBehind with a SrcIn tint, clipped)
3. Content: The thread drawn on top. (children (web) / content slot (Compose))

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Decorative: the pattern is a CSS ::before mask with no semantics; the wrapper is a plain div. Android: Decorative: drawn in drawBehind, so it adds no semantics node.
- Name. Web: None; the pattern is never announced. Android: None.
- Keyboard. Web: Not focusable; focus moves through the thread content only. Android: Not focusable; TalkBack moves through the content only.
- Touch target. Web: Not interactive; pointer-events: none keeps taps on the content. Android: Not interactive; the drawing does not take input.
- Contrast. Web: The pattern is 8% grey so it stays under text; text sits on the bubbles. Text placed straight on the wallpaper: text/primary 12.0:1, text/secondary 5.6:1 on #F5F5F6. Android: Same tokens, same ratios.
- State. Web: No state. Android: No state.
- Motion. Web: Static. Android: Static.

Example: Behind a thread
```tsx
<ChatWallpaper style={{ minHeight: '100%' }}>
  <MessageList>
    <DayDivider label="Today" />
    <ChatBubble kind="outgoing" sender="Equal AI" time="03:21">Hi, who is this?</ChatBubble>
    …
  </MessageList>
</ChatWallpaper>
```
```kotlin
ChatWallpaper(Modifier.fillMaxSize()) {
    Column(
        Modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(vertical = 16.dp),
        horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally,
        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp),
    ) {
        DayDivider("Today")
        ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Outgoing, sender = "Equal AI", timestamp = "03:21", message = "Hi, who is this?")
        ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Incoming, sender = "Dr Mehta Clinic", timestamp = "03:21",
            message = "This is Priya from Dr. Mehta's clinic. Your appointment is confirmed for tomorrow.")
    }
}
```

#### Equal call (`equal-call`)

Equal user to Equal user calls: the call screen (receiver and caller), Identified by Equal, swipe to answer, the in-app incoming strip (three options) and the ongoing strip, the heads-up stand-in and the Voice Call card. Reuses the vOIP call controls.

- React: `import { EqualCallScreen, SwipeToAnswer, IdentifiedByEqual, CallStrip, CallLogCard } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `EqualCallScreen`, `SwipeToAnswer`, `IdentifiedByEqual`, `IncomingCallStrip`, `OngoingCallStrip`, `IncomingCallNotification`, `CallLogCard`
- Tokens: `call-avatar/bg`, `call-avatar/text`, `call-control/subtle-bg`, `call-strip/bg`, `button/end-call`, `button/primary`, `notification/bg`
- Source: Equal To Equal Call Experience

Props of `SwipeToAnswer`:
- `onAccept?`: `() => void`. Drag Accept up 86, or tap it.
- `onDecline?`: `() => void`. Decline.
- `onMessage?`: `() => void`. Reply with a message.

Props of `IdentifiedByEqual`:
- `size?`: `'lg' | 'sm'` = 'lg'. body2 + 14 logo, or caption + 12 logo.

Props of `CallLogCard`:
- `duration`: `string`. "1min".
- `direction?`: `'outgoing' | 'incoming'` = 'outgoing'. call_made or call_received.

Do: Say who is calling and that Equal identified them. Keep the in-app strip option a prop. Let the assistant strip (OngoingCallBar) and the user call strip (CallStrip) stay separate.

Don't: Don't draw the heads-up or the permission dialog in the app; the OS does. Don't make the call icon tappable while a call is live.

Anatomy:
1. Header: Who, and that Equal identified them. (Large: headline name + Identified by (body2, 14 logo) · Compact: 40 subtle Minimise · subheading name + status · 40 Message (caller))
2. Avatar: The other person's initials. (200 call-avatar/bg disc · initials DM Sans 600 at 40 % · ripples 280 / 360 / 440 once connected)
3. Swipe to answer: Decline · Accept · Message. (52 circles: decline button/end-call, accept button/primary, message call-control/bg + stroke/subtle · captions body2 · chevrons 20 at 100 / 70 / 40 / 20 %)
4. Call strips: Incoming (3 options) or ongoing. (call-strip/bg · incoming 60 / 52 high, padding 16 / 24 · ongoing 72: 40 mute · subheading text/action name - time · 40 end)
5. Heads-up stand-in: Android's CallStyle notification. (radius 20 · notification/bg (dark) · 48 avatar + call-received badge · DECLINE / ANSWER system pills)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Accept, Decline, Message, Minimise and End are buttons; speaker / mute are switches; the incoming strip is one button; the ongoing strip is a group. Android: Same roles; Accept carries a custom "Answer" action for TalkBack.
- Name. Web: "Identified by Equal AI" is one node; the strip reads "Answer call from Keshav Reddy"; the ongoing label reads "Return to call with Keshav Reddy, 0:21". Android: Same strings via clearAndSetSemantics.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab order: header, then the bottom actions; Accept also answers on Enter. Android: D-pad in the same order.
- Touch target. Web: 52 circles; the 40 strip and header buttons sit in 44 targets. Android: 48dp via minimumInteractiveComponentSize.
- Contrast. Web: Decline icon on #E11D48 is 4.7:1; avatar initials 9.1:1 / 10.9:1; strip options 2 and 3 green on #F7F7F7 are 2.66:1 in light (option 1 passes). Android: Same tokens.
- State. Web: Calling… / Ringing… / Connecting... are announced politely; the timer is not. Android: liveRegion Polite on the status text.
- Motion. Web: The chevrons and ripples hold still under reduced motion; dragging Accept still works. Android: rememberReduceMotion() stops the chevron bob and the pulse.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Incoming strip options 2 and 3 fail AA in light (green on #F7F7F7, 2.66:1); keep option 1 as the default.

Example: Incoming call
```tsx
<EqualCallScreen role="receiver" state="ringing" name="Keshav Reddy" initials="KR" onAccept={answer} onDecline={decline} />
```
```kotlin
EqualCallScreen(
    role = EqualCallRole.Receiver,
    state = EqualCallState.Ringing,
    name = "Keshav Reddy",
    initials = "KR",
    onAccept = { /* answer */ },
    onDecline = { /* decline */ },
)
```

Example: Swipe to answer and badge
```tsx
<IdentifiedByEqual />
<SwipeToAnswer onAccept={answer} onDecline={decline} onMessage={reply} />
```
```kotlin
IdentifiedByEqual()
SwipeToAnswer(onAccept = { /* answer */ }, onDecline = { /* decline */ }, onMessage = { /* reply */ })
```

Example: Call strips
```tsx
<CallStrip state="incoming" style="avatar" name="Keshav Reddy" initials="KR" onAnswer={answer} />
<CallStrip state="incoming" style="icon" name="Keshav Reddy" />
<CallStrip state="incoming" style="accent" name="Keshav Reddy" />
<CallStrip state="ongoing" name="Keshav Reddy" seconds={21} onOpen={openCall} onEnd={end} />
```
```kotlin

IncomingCallStrip(name = "Keshav Reddy", style = CallStripStyle.Icon, onAnswer = {})
IncomingCallStrip(name = "Keshav Reddy", style = CallStripStyle.Accent, onAnswer = {})
OngoingCallStrip(name = "Keshav Reddy", seconds = 21, onOpen = { /* back to the call */ }, onEnd = { /* end */ })
```

Example: Heads-up stand-in and call card
```tsx
<IncomingCallNotification name="Keshav Reddy" initials="KR" />
<CallLogCard duration="1min" />
```
```kotlin

CallLogCard(duration = "1min")
```

#### Missed call card (`missed-call`)

The thread card for a call the assistant couldn’t pick up. One component, three cases: we know why the caller usually calls, we know only their name, or we know nothing. Every case ends in Call back.

- React: `import { MissedCallCard } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `MissedCallCard`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `missed-call/bg`, `missed-call/stroke`, `missed-call/icon-bg`, `missed-call/icon`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/action`, `stroke/subtle`

Do: Pick the case from what we know: reason + art, then name only, then unknown. Never invent a reason. Show thumbs only with a reason, since they rate the reason. Call back opens the same Call Back task as everywhere else (Flows → Call Back).

Don't: Don’t colour the whole card red; the warm tint says “missed”, not “error”. Don’t show caller art without a reason; the disc keeps the three cases distinct.

Anatomy:
1. Card: White card holding the head, reason and Call back. (width 320 (shrinks to fit) · bg/surface · radius lg (16) · gap 10 to the thumbs)
2. Head: Tinted strip that says the call was missed. (margin 6 · padding 10 / 12 · radius 12 · missed-call/bg · 1 px missed-call/stroke · gap 12)
3. Art or disc: Caller art with a missed badge (with a reason) or the red missed-call disc. (Asset category 48 · badge 20 missed-call/icon-bg with 2 px missed-call/bg ring · Icon phone-missed-fill 12 / 24 · missed-call/icon)
4. Title and why: "{caller} Called" or "Missed by the assistant", then why. (Text subheading text/primary, one line · Text body2 Regular text/secondary · time Text micro tabular text/secondary when there is no reason)
5. Likely calls for: Optional reason block with bold key words and the time. (padding 4 16 6 · gap 2 · Text overline text/secondary · body1 Regular text/secondary · time Text micro tabular text/primary)
6. Call back: Full-width action row. (48 high · 1 px stroke/subtle top · Icon call 20 · gap 8 · Text subheading · text/action)
7. Feedback thumbs: Optional 👍 / 👎 to rate the reason. (40 circles, 48 touch area · gap 8 · bg/surface · 1 px stroke/subtle · Icon thumb 20 text/secondary · on: filled icon + text/action icon and stroke)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Call back is a <button>; thumbs are <button aria-pressed> in a role="group"; art and icons are hidden (alt="", aria-hidden). Android: Call back is clickable(role = Role.Button); thumbs are toggleable(role = Role.Button); art and icons have null contentDescription.
- Name. Web: Call back from its visible label; thumbs aria-label "Helpful" / "Not helpful"; the group is "Was this helpful?". Android: Call back reads its label; thumb icons contentDescription "Helpful" / "Not helpful"; the thumbs Row has contentDescription "Was this helpful?".
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to Call back and each thumb; Enter/Space activates; pressing the selected thumb clears it. Android: TalkBack: swipe to Call back and the thumbs, double-tap to activate.
- Touch target. Web: The Call back row is 48 px high and full width; the 40 px thumbs use eq-touch for a 48 px hit area. Android: The Call back row is 48 dp; the 40 dp thumbs use touchTarget() for a 48 dp touch area.
- Contrast. Web: Title text/primary 12.4:1 and body text/secondary 5.7:1 on missed-call/bg; missed icon #DB330B on #FBEBE7 4.0:1. Call back and the selected thumb are text/action: brand green #00B140 on white is 2.85:1 (accepted brand decision); lime in dark is 13.7:1. Android: Same tokens; dark missed icon #FF8A6B on #45302C 5.3:1.
- State. Web: Thumb selection uses aria-pressed and swaps the outline icon for a filled one plus a green stroke, so not colour alone. Android: toggleable exposes on / off; the icon also swaps to filled.
- Motion. Web: eq-pressable scale on press; transitions go to 0 ms under prefers-reduced-motion via base.css. Android: eqPressFeedback on press only.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision: the Call back label and the selected thumb use text/action #00B140 on white (2.85:1), below 4.5:1 for text in light (MissedCall.css, MissedCall.kt).

Example: With a reason
```tsx
<MissedCallCard
  caller="Kuldeep Solanki" category="real-estate"
  reason={<>Promote <b>L&amp;T Realty residential</b> projects.</>}
  time="03:21" onCallBack={callBack}
  feedback={feedback} onFeedback={setFeedback} />
```
```kotlin
EqualTheme {
    var feedback by remember { mutableStateOf<CallFeedback?>(null) }
    MissedCallCard(
        caller = "Kuldeep Solanki",
        category = EqualCategory.RealEstate,
        reason = buildAnnotatedString {
            append("Promote ")
            withStyle(SpanStyle(fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold)) { append("L&T Realty residential") }
            append(" projects.")
        },
        time = "03:21",
        onCallBack = { /* call back */ },
        feedback = feedback,
        onFeedback = { feedback = it },
    )
}
```

Example: Caller unknown
```tsx
<MissedCallCard time="3:31 PM" onCallBack={callBack} />
```
```kotlin
EqualTheme {
    MissedCallCard(time = "3:31 PM", onCallBack = { /* call back */ })
}
```

Example: Name only
```tsx
<MissedCallCard caller="Valluri" time="3:31 PM" onCallBack={callBack} />
```
```kotlin
EqualTheme {
    MissedCallCard(caller = "Valluri", time = "3:31 PM", onCallBack = { /* call back */ })
}
```

### Group: Display

#### Avatars (`avatars`)

Every face in the app: caller category art or initials for contacts, the Equal orb for the assistant, the ringed 3D profile avatar for the user, and the robot mascot.

- React: `import { ContactAvatar, CategoryAvatar, AiAvatar, EqualOrb, ProfileAvatar, Mascot } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `ContactAvatar`, `CategoryAvatar`, `InitialsAvatar`, `AiAvatar`, `EqualLogoOrb`, `ProfileAvatar`, `EqualMascot`
- Tokens: `action-card/highlight`, `text/action`, `button/primary`, `text/on-action`, `bg/surface`
- Source: Icons, emoji, categories, logo · §12 AI Assistant Avatar

Do: Default unknown callers to `na` and incoming bubbles to `others` (the red telephone). Size ProfileAvatar by width only; its height follows so the head can rise above the ring. Use AiAvatar at 24 / 36 / 48 only.

Don't: Never crop category art or the profile avatar; the circle and ring are part of the image. Don't draw your own green circle for the assistant; the orb swaps light (#00B140) and dark (lime) files by theme. Don't use initials for business callers; they get their category art.

Anatomy:
1. ContactAvatar: image or disc: Category art for unknown callers, or a tinted disc with initials for saved contacts. (48 list · 36 header · 96 contact info · circle · Asset category image, or one of 6 tones contact-avatar/*-bg picked from the initials)
2. ContactAvatar: initials: First two letters, uppercased. (Text atom · subheading at Medium, 37.5% of size (18 at 48) · contact-avatar/*-text)
3. ContactAvatar: saved badge: Person badge marking a known contact. (36% of size · contact-avatar/badge-bg + person icon contact-avatar/badge-icon at 70% · bottom-right, offset 10%)
4. ContactAvatar: selected check: Green tick that replaces the saved badge in selection mode. (web 18 + 2 bg/surface ring, Compose 22 incl. 2dp bg/surface ring · button/primary · check 12 text/on-action)
5. AiAvatar / EqualOrb: The Equal orb for the assistant; light and dark files swap with the theme. (24 / 36 / 48 (FAB 58) · image drawn at size / 0.8, glow overflows)
6. ProfileAvatar: The user's 3D character, gold ring when paid. (width 72 default · height ≈ 1.12 × width · paid = gold-ringed art, free = bust art)
7. Mascot: Robot for the assistant toggle card. (40 default (36 on the toggle) · dimmed = greyscale at 70%)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: EqualOrb, Mascot, the saved badge and the selected check are role='img'; CategoryAvatar and ProfileAvatar are <img>; the initials disc is plain text. Android: Image with contentDescription; InitialsAvatar is text plus a 'Saved contact' badge node; SelectedCheckBadge is an icon described 'Selected'.
- Name. Web: Orb 'Equal AI', Mascot 'Equal assistant', ProfileAvatar 'Your profile', CategoryAvatar the category label, saved badge 'Saved contact', check 'Selected'. Pass label = '' when a visible name sits beside it. Android: Same defaults via contentDescription; pass null when the row already names the person.
- Keyboard. Web: Not focusable; avatars are read with the row or header that holds them. Android: Not focusable on their own; TalkBack reads them inside the parent's merged node.
- Touch target. Web: Not interactive; the row or button around the avatar owns the target. Android: Not interactive; the parent row owns the target.
- Contrast. Web: The six initials tones are 4.7–6.5:1 in light and 4.7–8.7:1 in dark. The selected check is white on #00B140 (2.85:1) in light. Android: Same tokens as web.
- State. Web: Selected swaps the saved badge for a tick shape announced as 'Selected'. Mascot dimmed is visual only; the toggle beside it states on or off. Android: Selected is announced as 'Selected' via the check's contentDescription.
- Motion. Web: Mascot filter and opacity fade over 200ms; zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: None.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision: Avatar.tsx / Foundation.kt the selected check is white on button/primary #00B140, 2.85:1 in light mode, below 3:1.
- Avatar.tsx / Foundation.kt: ContactAvatar has no label / contentDescription pass-through, so its CategoryAvatar always announces the category name, even beside a visible name (ChatHeader, ChatListItem).

Example: Profile avatar: free vs paid
```tsx
<ProfileAvatar variant="male" size={70} tier="free" />
<ProfileAvatar variant="male" size={70} tier="paid" />
```
```kotlin
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(24.dp)) {
    ProfileAvatar(variant = ProfileAvatarVariant.Male, width = 70.dp, tier = PlanTier.Free)
    ProfileAvatar(variant = ProfileAvatarVariant.Male, width = 70.dp, tier = PlanTier.Paid)
}
```

Example: Caller categories
```tsx
<CategoryAvatar category="na" />
<CategoryAvatar category="delivery" />
<CategoryAvatar category="real-estate" size={48} />
```
```kotlin

    CategoryAvatar(category = EqualCategory.NA, size = 48.dp)
    CategoryAvatar(category = EqualCategory.Delivery, size = 48.dp)

}
```

Example: Contact avatar
```tsx
<ContactAvatar />
<ContactAvatar category="others" />
<ContactAvatar initials="AN" />
<ContactAvatar initials="AN" selected />
<ContactAvatar category="career" size={36} />
```

```tsx

```
```kotlin
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(14.dp), verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
    // The tone is picked from the initials by default; pass tone to choose.
    listOf("AN", "AR", "KS", "PR", "VJ", "MS").zip(ContactTone.entries).forEach { (initials, tone) ->
        InitialsAvatar(initials = initials, size = 48.dp, tone = tone)
    }
}
```

```kotlin
    AiAvatar(size = AiAvatarSize.Small)
    AiAvatar(size = AiAvatarSize.Medium)
    AiAvatar(size = AiAvatarSize.Large)
```
