Example: Expiry chips
```tsx
<ExpiryChip tone="active">25th Jun ’26</ExpiryChip>
<ExpiryChip tone="warning">03 Days</ExpiryChip>
<ExpiryChip tone="danger">Today</ExpiryChip>
```
```kotlin
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(10.dp)) {
    ExpiryChip(text = "25th Jun ’26", tone = ExpiryTone.Active)
    ExpiryChip(text = "03 Days", tone = ExpiryTone.Warning)
    ExpiryChip(text = "Today", tone = ExpiryTone.Danger)
}
```

### Group: Navigation

#### App bar (`app-bar`)

The standard screen header with back, a subheading title and trailing actions, plus the uppercase section header that labels groups of rows.

- React: `import { AppBar, SectionHeader } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `EqualAppBar`, `SectionHeader`
- Tokens: `bg/primary`, `bg/surface`, `shadow/header`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`
- Source: Surfaces from the Typography screen inventory · App Bar, Section Header

Do: Centre the title in flow screens (Personal Details, Your Addresses, Contact Info). Keep SectionHeader side inset equal to the RowGroup inset below it (20 on the You tab).

Don't: Don't write section headers in capitals in source; pass normal text and let the component uppercase it. Don't put a filled Button in the app bar; trailing actions are icon or text buttons.

Anatomy:
1. Container: Header surface at the top of a screen. (center 56 high · start 64 high · padding 4 start / 8 end (start without back: 16) · bg/primary default, bg/surface or transparent · elevated adds shadow/header)
2. Status bar: Optional mock status bar on the same background. (52 high · statusBar prop)
3. Back button: Ghost icon button that goes back. (arrow-back 24 · web 40 + eq-touch 48, Compose 48 · text/primary)
4. Title: Screen name, one line, centred by default. (Text atom · subheading 16/500 · text/primary · ellipsis · centre uses equal side columns · start gap 8 after back)
5. Trailing actions: Optional actions at the end. (`trailing` / `actions` slot)
6. SectionHeader: Uppercase region label with an optional action. (overline 11/500 text/secondary · padding 24 top / 12 bottom / inset 20 · label size 13/18 Medium text/secondary, 30 / 18 · Compose action buttonSmall text/action with a 48 target)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: <header> with the title as <h1>; SectionHeader renders an <h2> by default (`as` sets h3 / h4 / span). Android: Column/Row; the title and the SectionHeader text have semantics { heading() }.
- Name. Web: Back is IconButton label 'Back'; the h1 text names the screen; SectionHeader sets aria-label to the sentence-case title so it is not read letter by letter. Android: PlainIconButton contentDescription 'Back'; the title text names the screen.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab reaches Back, then trailing actions; screen-reader users can jump to the h1 and section headings. Android: TalkBack: swipe through Back, title and actions; heading navigation finds the title and section headers.
- Touch target. Web: Back is 40px with .eq-touch for 48px. Android: PlainIconButton is 48dp with minimumInteractiveComponentSize(); the SectionHeader action gets a 48dp area via touchTarget().
- Contrast. Web: Title text/primary 12.3:1 on bg/primary; SectionHeader text/secondary 5.7:1. Android: Same tokens; a SectionHeader action in text/action #00B140 is 2.85:1 on white.
- State. Web: None beyond the controls it holds; the title is static text. Android: None beyond the controls it holds.
- Motion. Web: Back button press scale via .eq-pressable; zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: None; PlainIconButton uses the default indication.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision: Rows.kt the SectionHeader action label text/action #00B140 is 2.85:1 in light mode, below 4.5:1 for 12sp text.

Example: Centred (flows)
```tsx
<AppBar title="Personal Details" onBack={goBack} />
```
```kotlin
EqualAppBar(title = "Personal Details", onBackClick = {})
```

Example: Start-aligned, elevated, with trailing
```tsx
<AppBar title="Active Instructions" align="start" surface="surface" elevated
  onBack={goBack} trailing={<TextButton leadingIcon="add">Add</TextButton>} />
```
```kotlin
EqualAppBar(
    title = "Active Instructions",
    onBackClick = {},
    align = AppBarAlign.Start,
    background = EqualTheme.colors.bgSurface,
    elevated = true,
) {
    EqualTextButton(text = "Add", onClick = {}, leadingIcon = EqualIcons.Add)
}
```

Example: Section headers
```tsx
<SectionHeader>Your assistant</SectionHeader>
<SectionHeader qualifier="(Optional)">Guiding direction</SectionHeader>
<SectionHeader action={<TextButton size="small">Clear all</TextButton>}>
  Recommended for you
</SectionHeader>
```
```kotlin

// Compose: no `qualifier` slot; it is appended to the title (and uppercased with it).

```

#### Bottom nav (`bottom-nav`)

The floating two-tab pill (Chats, You) with an unread count, beside the Equal orb FAB that opens the assistant.

- React: `import { BottomNav, Fab } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `BottomNavBar`, `EqualFab`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `shadow/nav`, `nav/selected-bg`, `text/action`, `text/secondary`, `button/primary`, `text/on-action`
- Source: §4 Tab Bar (Bottom Navigation)

Do: Float the nav over content and leave ~104dp bottom padding so the last row is reachable. Pass the user's gender as `avatar` so the You tab matches the profile avatar.

Don't: Don't add a third tab; the pill is Chats and You. Don't replace the FAB orb with an icon; the orb carries its own glow.

Anatomy:
1. Pill container: Floating surface that holds the two tabs. (padding 8 · radius full · bg/surface · shadow/nav)
2. Tab item: One destination capsule; the selected one is filled. (web 84 × 56, Compose 99 × 52 · radius full · selected nav/selected-bg)
3. Icon: Chats bubble (filled when selected) or the user's ProfileAvatar. (Icon atom 24 · selected text/action · unselected text/secondary · avatar 24 wide, lifted 3)
4. Count badge: Unread count on the Chats icon. (16 · 1.5 bg/surface ring · button/primary · badgeCount text/on-action · web 99+, Compose 9+)
5. Label: Tab name under the icon. (Text atom · caption 12/500 · gap 2 · selected text/action · unselected text/secondary)
6. Fab: The Equal orb button beside the pill that opens the assistant. (58 · gap 16 · orb image carries its glow)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: <nav aria-label='Main'> with <button> items; the current one has aria-current='page'. Fab is a <button>. Android: selectableGroup() on the pill and selectable(role = Role.Tab) per item; EqualFab is clickable(role = Role.Button).
- Name. Web: Item text plus contents: 'Chats' plus visually hidden 'N unread', and 'You' (the avatar is decorative). Fab aria-label 'Talk to Equal AI'. Android: Merged text: 'N unread' then 'Chats'; the You avatar has contentDescription = null. Fab 'Ask Equal AI'.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab through Chats, You, Fab; Enter or Space activates. Focus draws the solid 1.5 px stroke/focus outline (no black ring). Android: TalkBack: swipe between tabs, announces 'selected', 'tab' and the position; double-tap to switch.
- Touch target. Web: Items 84 × 56, Fab 58. Android: Items 99 × 52, Fab 58.
- Contrast. Web: Unselected label text/secondary on white 5.7:1; selected text/action #00B140 on nav/selected-bg (green at 4%) is 2.7:1 in light; dark lime on the lime-tinted capsule is 11.2:1. Android: Same tokens as web.
- State. Web: aria-current='page'; selection also fills the capsule and switches the chat icon to filled, not colour alone. Android: selected semantics from selectable; the capsule fill and icon change too.
- Motion. Web: Capsule fill and colour fade over 200ms; Fab press scale; zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: Fab press scale via eqPressFeedback; tab switch is instant.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision: BottomNav.css / BottomNavBar.kt selected label text/action #00B140 on nav/selected-bg is 2.7:1 in light mode, below 4.5:1.
- BottomNav.tsx / BottomNavBar.kt: Fab names differ ('Talk to Equal AI' on web, 'Ask Equal AI' on Android).
- BottomNavBar.kt: EqualFab uses indication = null with no focus ring, so hardware-keyboard focus on it is invisible.

Example: Interactive
```tsx
const [tab, setTab] = useState<NavTab>('chats');

<BottomNav active={tab} onChange={setTab} unread={7} />
```
```kotlin
var tab by remember { mutableStateOf(EqualTab.Chats) }

BottomNavBar(
    selectedTab = tab,
    onTabSelected = { tab = it },
    onFabClick = {},
    chatsBadgeCount = 7,
)
```

Example: You active, female avatar, no FAB
```tsx
<BottomNav active="you" avatar="female" showFab={false} />
```
```kotlin
// Compose: BottomNavBar always draws the FAB; there is no showFab = false.
BottomNavBar(
    selectedTab = EqualTab.You,
    onTabSelected = {},
    onFabClick = {},
    avatar = ProfileAvatarVariant.Female,
)
```

Example: FAB on its own
```tsx
<Fab onClick={openAssistant} />
```
```kotlin
EqualFab(onClick = {})
```

#### Chat header (`chat-header`)

Headers for the chat surfaces: the in-conversation header (with the Takeover pill on a live call), the chat-list selection header, and the home header with the assistant toggle.

- React: `import { ChatHeader, TakeoverPill, SelectionHeader, HomeHeader } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `ChatHeader`, `TakeoverPill`, `SelectionChatHeader`, `HomeHeader`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `bg/primary`, `shadow/header`, `gradient/takeover`, `takeover/text`, `takeover/stroke`, `action/stroke/unread`, `shadow/glass`, `text/action`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `button/danger`
- Source: §5 Chat Header (In-Conversation)

Do: Show the phone number as the subtitle normally and a status line ("You have a visitor") during a live call. During a live call show only the Takeover pill; the call and more buttons go away. Route selection-mode Delete through the delete confirm sheet.

Don't: Don't show Takeover alongside the call button; that is two actions for the same intent. Don't truncate the phone number with custom styles; it is tabular and one line.

Anatomy:
1. Container: White header at the top of a conversation. (64 high · bg/surface · shadow/header · padding web 4 start / 8 end, gap 4 · Compose h12)
2. Back button: Goes back to the chat list. (arrow-back 24 · web 36 + eq-touch 48, Compose 48 · text/primary)
3. Avatar: Contact or category avatar, or the orb for Equal AI's own chat. (36 · ContactAvatar or AiAvatar)
4. Name and subtitle: Who the chat is with, and a phone number or status line. (name subheading 16/500 text/primary · subtitle caption Regular 12/400 text/secondary, tabular for numbers · web 10, Compose 12 after the avatar)
5. Trailing actions: Call and More options, or the Takeover pill on a live call. (call + more-vert 24 · web 36 + eq-touch, Compose 48)
6. TakeoverPill: Glass pill that takes over a live call. (34 high · padding h14 · gradient/takeover · 1px takeover/stroke · shadow/glass · call-filled 18 + button 14/500 takeover/text · 48 target)
7. SelectionHeader: Selection-mode bar: count, Mark read, Delete, then Select All. (row 64 · 'N Selected' subheading · Mark read 26 high pill, 1px action/stroke/unread, done-all 16 text/action + buttonSmall text/primary · delete button/danger · Select All row 40 (48 target) with checkbox + bodyLarge)
8. HomeHeader: Status bar, TopBar and the assistant toggle card on bg/primary. (bg/primary · shadow/header · toggle card padding 0 12 12)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: <header> with IconButtons; the name is an <h1>. Takeover and Mark read are <button>s. Android: Row with PlainIconButtons (Role.Button); the name has semantics { heading() }.
- Name. Web: 'Back', 'Call', 'More options'; Takeover and Mark read use visible text; selection back is 'Exit selection'; the home toggle switch is 'AI Assistant'. Android: 'Back', 'Call', 'More options', 'Delete'; Takeover and Mark read by text; selection back is 'Back'; the home toggle card reads its title and description as one switch.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab order: Back, Call, More (or Takeover); in selection mode Back, Mark read, Delete, Select All. Focus draws the solid 1.5 px stroke/focus outline (no black ring). Android: TalkBack: swipe in the same order; the Select All row is one checkbox node. Takeover and Mark read show no hardware-keyboard focus.
- Touch target. Web: 36px buttons get 48px via .eq-touch, but with a 4px gap the Call and More hit areas overlap by 8px; Takeover, Mark read and Select All use .eq-touch. Android: Icon buttons 48dp; TakeoverPill and MarkReadPill use minimumInteractiveComponentSize(); the Select All row is 40dp with a 48dp touch area.
- Contrast. Web: Name 12.6:1, subtitle text/secondary 5.7:1; Takeover takeover/text #009837 on #E4FFED is 3.6:1 in light, white on #212615 in dark 15.5:1; delete #C50000 6.2:1. Android: Same tokens as web.
- State. Web: Live call is shown by Takeover replacing Call and More; the 'N Selected' count has role='status', so changes are announced. Android: Select All exposes checked state via toggleable(Role.Checkbox); the count is a polite live region.
- Motion. Web: Press scale on buttons and pills; zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: eqPressFeedback on pills, following the system animator scale.

Known accessibility gaps:
- ChatHeader.tsx: the 36px Call and More buttons sit 4px apart, so their 48px eq-touch hit areas overlap by 8px.
- ChatHeader.css / ChatHeader.kt: TakeoverPill label takeover/text #009837 on gradient/takeover #E4FFED is 3.6:1 in light mode, below 4.5:1 for 14px Medium text.
- ChatHeader.tsx / ChatHeader.kt: the selection back button is 'Exit selection' on web but 'Back' on Android.
- ChatHeader.kt: TakeoverPill and MarkReadPill use indication = null with no focus ring, so hardware-keyboard focus is invisible.

Example: Default
```tsx

  avatar={{ initials: 'AN' }} onBack={goBack} onCall={call} onMore={openInfo} />
```
```kotlin

    name = "Amit Nanda",
    subtitle = "+91 98717 46113",
    initials = "AN",
    onBackClick = {},
    onCallClick = {},
    onMoreClick = {},
)
```

```tsx
  onBack={goBack} onTakeover={takeover} />
```

```kotlin
    variant = ChatHeaderVariant.LiveCall,
    onBackClick = {},
```

#### Status bar (`status-bar`)

The Material 3 Android status bar (52dp: Roboto time; wifi, triangle signal and an upright battery) for mocks, flows and screen demos.

- React: `import { StatusBar } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `StatusBar`
- Tokens: `bg/primary`, `text/primary`
- Source: §1 Status Bar

Do: Use it only in mocks and flow demos; the app draws edge-to-edge and pads with `WindowInsets.statusBars`. Match `background` to the surface beneath (bg/surface under white headers).

Don't: Don't add carrier names or extra icons; the Material 3 bar is time + wifi + signal + battery.

Anatomy:
1. Container: Full-width strip at the top of a mock screen. (52 high · padding h24 · bg/primary default (match the header))
2. Time: Clock text on the left. (system font (Roboto) Medium 14/20 · tracking 0.1 · tabular · text/primary (or `color`))
3. System icons: Wifi, signal and battery on the right. (Icon atoms 18 each · gap 4 · order wifi, signal, battery · same colour as the time)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Plain <div> with aria-hidden, so the whole mock is hidden from screen readers. Android: Row with clearAndSetSemantics {}, so TalkBack skips it.
- Name. Web: None: it is a mock of system chrome and the fake '12:30' is not read. Android: None; real apps draw under the system bar with WindowInsets.statusBars.
- Keyboard. Web: Nothing focusable. Android: Nothing focusable.
- Touch target. Web: Not interactive. Android: Not interactive.
- Contrast. Web: text/primary on bg/primary is 12.3:1 in light and 11.9:1 in dark (white at 80% on #141414); a custom `color` must keep 4.5:1. Android: Same tokens; the `color` parameter must keep 4.5:1 on `background`.
- State. Web: None; the time and icons are static. Android: None; the time and icons are static.
- Motion. Web: None. Android: None.

Example: Default
```tsx
<StatusBar />
```
```kotlin
StatusBar()
```

Example: On a white header

#### Top bar (`top-bar`)

The Chats home bar: the vector Equal AI logo with the plan marker, plus the logo and mark on their own.

- React: `import { TopBar, EqualLogo, EqualMark } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `TopBar`, `EqualLogo`, `EqualMark`
- Tokens: `text/action`, `gradient/gold`, `text/on-dark`
- Source: §2 Top Bar (Logo + Availability Status)

Do: Use the vector logo in text/action so it is #00B140 in light and lime in dark. Keep the logo 20dp high in the top bar.

Don't: Don't use a raster logo; the logo is coded as vector paths. Don't stretch or recolour the lockup outside text/action.

Anatomy:
1. Container: Home bar holding the logo, plan marker and trailing actions. (56 high · padding h16 · gap 8 · transparent on bg/primary)
2. EqualLogo: Six-dot mark plus 'equal ai' wordmark. (20 high · 113:24 aspect · text/action (#00B140 light, lime dark))
3. PlanBadge: Plan marker after the logo. (16 high · radius/xs 4 · gradient/gold + text/on-dark, or expired gradient/expired-badge over plan-badge/expired-bg + white)
4. Trailing slot: Optional actions at the end, e.g. search. (pushed right by a flex spacer)
5. EqualMark: The six-dot mark alone. (width 23 default · 488:428 aspect · text/action)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Plain <div>; EqualLogo is an <svg role='img'>; EqualMark is aria-hidden unless given a title. Android: Row; EqualLogo is an Image; EqualMark contentDescription defaults to null.
- Name. Web: Logo reads 'Equal AI', then the badge text ('UNLIMITED' or 'PLAN EXPIRED'). Trailing buttons need their own labels. Android: EqualLogo contentDescription 'Equal AI', then the PlanBadge text.
- Keyboard. Web: Nothing focusable except what you put in `trailing`. Android: TalkBack: logo and badge are read in order; trailing actions are focusable.
- Touch target. Web: The bar itself is not interactive; trailing actions bring their own 48px targets. Android: Not interactive; trailing actions bring their own 48dp targets.
- Contrast. Web: The logo is exempt as a logotype. PlanBadge white on gradient/gold is 3.0–4.2:1 and the expired badge 2.4–6.9:1 (both fail 4.5:1 at 10sp). Android: Same tokens as web.
- State. Web: Plan state is in the badge text, not colour alone. Android: Same.
- Motion. Web: None. Android: None.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision (premium gold, subscription surfaces only): topBar.tsx / HomeChrome.kt: the paid PlanBadge has white text on gradient/gold at 3.0–4.2:1, below 4.5:1.
- TopBar.tsx / HomeChrome.kt: the expired PlanBadge's white label drops to 2.4:1 on the #E4918C middle stop of gradient/expired-badge.

Example: Default


```kotlin
}
```


### Group: Overlays

#### Bottom sheet (`bottom-sheet`)

Sheets that rise over the current screen: the standard sheet with a floating close or title row, the centred confirm content for destructive actions, and the full-height sheet for the instruction setup chat.

- React: `import { BottomSheet, ConfirmSheetContent, FullSheet } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `EqualBottomSheet`, `ConfirmSheetContent`, `FullSheet`
- Tokens: `bg/overlay`, `bg/primary`, `bg/surface`, `shadow/raised`, `text/secondary`, `text/primary`, `button/danger`, `text/on-danger`, `chat/wallpaper-bg`
- Source: §17 Bottom Sheet

Do: Name the thing being deleted in the title and put its number in `subject` ("Delete chat with Amit Nanda", "(+91 9871746113)"). State the consequence in the body ("This action cannot be undone."). Render overlays inside a positioned container such as PhoneFrame; use mode="inline" in docs.

Don't: Don't put a Cancel button next to the confirm; the close button and scrim are the revise path. Don't use a sheet for a quick yes/no that needs no context; use a Dialog. Don't show both a title row and the floating close.

Anatomy:
1. Scrim: Dims the screen. Tapping it closes the sheet. (bg/overlay #1E1E1E @ 40% · fades over duration-slow web, motion.base Compose)
2. Sheet container: Panel anchored to the bottom that holds the content and scrolls when tall. (bg/primary · radius 32 top (24 with a title) · padding 24/24/28 web, 24 Compose (+ nav-bar inset) · max height 92%)
3. Close button: Floating close in the top-right corner, shown when there is no title. (IconButton neutral 44 · bg/surface · shadow/raised · close 22 text/secondary · inset 16 web / 12 Compose)
4. Title row: Optional row: close (X) on the left and a centred title. It replaces the floating close. (grid 40 / 1fr / 40 web, 48 + 1fr + 48 Compose · subheading text/primary · centred · close ghost 40 web, 48 Compose)
5. ConfirmSheetContent: illustration: Centred 3D illustration above the confirm text. (Asset 72dp · illustration-trash by default · decorative)
6. ConfirmSheetContent: title, subject, body: Names the thing affected, then the consequence. (title token text/primary, 20 above · subject body1 text/secondary tabular · body body1 text/secondary, 12 above)
7. ConfirmSheetContent: confirm button: One full-width commit, danger with the trash icon when destructive. (Button lg block · 45 high · 28 above · button/danger + text/on-danger · delete icon 18)
8. FullSheet: header and body: Full-height variant: orb, title and close over the chat wallpaper, with an optional pinned footer. (top 72 · radius 24 top · bg/surface · header padding 14/14/14/16, gap 10 · orb 32 · close neutral 40 web / 44 Compose · 1dp stroke/subtle below · body chat/wallpaper-bg · footer padding 8/16/16)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: The sheet is role="dialog" (aria-modal in overlay mode). The title row and the ConfirmSheetContent title are h2. FullSheet is a section with role="dialog"; its title is a plain span. Android: EqualBottomSheet and FullSheet set paneTitle on the panel. The title row, the FullSheet title and the ConfirmSheetContent title are heading(). The scrim is Role.Button with onClickLabel 'Dismiss'.
- Name. Web: aria-label is the title, or the label prop (default 'Sheet'); FullSheet uses its title. Close buttons are 'Close'. The FullSheet orb is decorative. Android: paneTitle is the title, or 'Bottom sheet', so TalkBack announces the sheet when it opens. Close icons have contentDescription 'Close'.
- Keyboard. Web: useModal moves focus into the sheet, traps Tab, makes the screen behind inert, closes on Escape and returns focus to the trigger. A scrim click also calls onClose. Android: EqualBackHandler: system Back calls onDismissRequest while visible. TalkBack: swipe to Close and double-tap, or double-tap the scrim.
- Touch target. Web: Close IconButtons (44 or 40) and the lg confirm button (45) all use eq-touch, so each hit area is at least 48. Android: EqualIconButton, PlainIconButton (48dp) and EqualButton apply minimumInteractiveComponentSize.
- Contrast. Web: Body text/secondary on bg/primary is 5.7:1 in light and 7.1:1 in dark; titles 12.3:1. Danger text/on-danger on button/danger is 6.2:1 light and 6.6:1 dark. A non-destructive primary confirm is white on green, 2.85:1 in light (accepted brand decision). Android: Same tokens and ratios. In dark the primary confirm is black on lime (17.4:1).
- State. Web: A closed overlay is aria-hidden, inert and visibility:hidden (BottomSheet and FullSheet), so its controls leave the Tab order. Android: Visibility comes from AnimatedVisibility; the panel leaves the tree when closed.
- Motion. Web: The sheet slides up and the scrim fades over duration-slow; the base.css reduced-motion rule sets the transitions to 0ms. Android: Scrim fade motion.base, slide in motion.slow (FullSheet motion.slow both ways); all skipped under rememberReduceMotion().

Known accessibility gaps:
- EqualBottomSheet (BottomSheet.kt) and FullSheet (Flows.kt): the screen behind the scrim stays in the TalkBack swipe order while the sheet is open.
- FullSheet in Flows.tsx: the header title is a plain span, not a heading (BottomSheet.tsx and the Compose FullSheet use one).
- Accepted brand decision: primary buttons put text/on-action white on button/primary #00B140 in light mode, 2.85:1 for 14sp text (Button.css / Buttons.kt). Dark (black on lime) is 17.4:1.

Example: Delete confirm (inline)
```tsx
<BottomSheet open mode="inline">
  <ConfirmSheetContent
    title={<>Delete chat with<br />Amit Nanda</>}
    subject="(+91 9871746113)"
    body="All past conversations will be deleted. This action cannot be undone."
    confirmLabel="Delete"
    destructive />
</BottomSheet>
```
```kotlin
// Compose: no inline mode; the sheet always draws over its parent with the scrim
EqualBottomSheet(visible = true, onDismissRequest = {}) {
    ConfirmSheetContent(
        title = "Delete chat with\nAmit Nanda",
        phone = "(+91 9871746113)",
        body = "All past conversations will be deleted. This action cannot be undone.",
        confirmLabel = "Delete",
        destructive = true,
        onConfirm = {},
    )
}
```

Example: Titled sheet (inline)
```tsx
<BottomSheet open mode="inline" title="Turn off WhatsApp updates?">
  <IllustrationHeader asset="illustration-whatsapp" size={120} />
  …
  <Button block size="lg">Turn off updates</Button>
</BottomSheet>
```
```kotlin
// Compose: no inline mode; the sheet always draws over its parent with the scrim
EqualBottomSheet(visible = true, onDismissRequest = {}, title = "Turn off WhatsApp updates?") {
    Column(horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally) {
        IllustrationHeader(asset = EqualAssets.IllustrationWhatsapp, size = 120.dp)
        EqualText(
            text = "You'll stop getting call alerts and account updates on WhatsApp.",
            style = EqualTheme.type.body1,
            color = EqualTheme.colors.textSecondary,
            textAlign = TextAlign.Center,
        )
        EqualButton(text = "Turn off updates", onClick = {}, size = EqualButtonSize.Block, modifier = Modifier.padding(top = 16.dp))
    }
}
```

Example: Overlay in a phone
```tsx
<PhoneFrame height={560}>
  <Button variant="danger" leadingIcon="delete" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Delete chat</Button>
  <BottomSheet open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
    <ConfirmSheetContent title={<>Delete chat with<br />Amit Nanda</>}
      subject="(+91 9871746113)" confirmLabel="Delete" destructive
      onConfirm={deleteChat} />
  </BottomSheet>
</PhoneFrame>
```
```kotlin
var open by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
Box(Modifier.fillMaxSize()) {
    EqualButton(text = "Delete chat", onClick = { open = true }, variant = EqualButtonVariant.Danger, leadingIcon = EqualIcons.Delete)
    EqualBottomSheet(visible = open, onDismissRequest = { open = false }) {
        ConfirmSheetContent(
            title = "Delete chat with\nAmit Nanda",
            phone = "(+91 9871746113)",
            // Compose: body is required
            body = "All past conversations will be deleted. This action cannot be undone.",
            confirmLabel = "Delete",
            destructive = true,
            onConfirm = { open = false },
        )
    }
}
```

Example: Full sheet
```tsx
<FullSheet open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} title="Setting up instruction"
  footer={
    <ChipRow gap={8}>
      <LargeActionChip emoji="✍️" label="Edit" state="read" />
      <LargeActionChip emoji="👍" label="Confirm" onClick={confirm} />
    </ChipRow>
  }>
  <MessageList>…</MessageList>
</FullSheet>
```
```kotlin

```

#### Context menu (`context-menu`)

The long-press menu of icon + label items, and OverflowMenu, the ⋮ button that opens one anchored to a card.

- React: `import { ContextMenu, OverflowMenu } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `ContextMenu`, `ContextMenuPopup`, `OverflowMenu`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `shadow/card`, `stroke/subtle`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/danger`
- Source: §18 Context Menu (Long-press)

Do: Put the destructive item last and mark it `danger`. Name the object in destructive labels ("Delete instruction", "Delete address").

Don't: Don't put more than four or five items in a menu. Don't delete straight from the menu; open the confirm sheet.

Anatomy:
1. Container: Floating surface that holds the menu items. (bg/surface · radius 12 · shadow/card · min width 131 (168 in OverflowMenu))
2. Item: One full-width row per action. (40 high web / 48 Compose · padding 0 16 0 12 web, h12 Compose · gap 10)
3. Item icon: Leading glyph for the action. (Icon 16 · text/secondary (text/danger when danger))
4. Item label: Verb naming the action, e.g. 'Delete instruction'. (body1 · text/primary (text/danger when danger))
5. Divider: Hairline between items. (1dp · stroke/subtle)
6. OverflowMenu: trigger: The ⋮ button that opens the menu anchored to a card. (IconButton ghost 32 · more-vert 20 text/primary · 48 touch area · menu 30 below, 6 in from the right)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: The container is role="menu" and each item is a button with role="menuitem". The ⋮ trigger has aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded. Android: Items are clickable Rows with Role.Button. OverflowMenu opens a focusable Popup. The trigger is Role.Button with stateDescription Expanded / Collapsed.
- Name. Web: Items are named by their visible label (icons are aria-hidden). The menu and trigger use the label prop (default 'More options'); AddressCard passes '{label} options' and InstructionCard '{title} options'. Android: Item labels are their text. The trigger contentDescription defaults to 'More options' and uses the same per-card strings.
- Keyboard. Web: Enter/Space or ArrowDown/Up on ⋮ opens the menu and focuses the first item. Arrow keys, Home and End move between items (roving tabIndex). Escape or choosing an item closes it and returns focus to ⋮; Tab or an outside click closes it. Android: The Popup is focusable, so Back or a tap outside dismisses it. TalkBack: swipe through the items, double-tap to select. The menu closes before onSelect runs.
- Touch target. Web: Items are 40px tall with no eq-touch. The 32px trigger gets 48 through IconButton's eq-touch. Android: Items are 48dp tall. The 32dp trigger uses touchTarget() for a 48dp area.
- Contrast. Web: Labels text/primary 12.6:1, icons text/secondary 5.7:1, danger text/danger 6.2:1 on white. Dark: 10.9:1, 6.7:1 and 5.1:1 on #1F1F1F. Android: Same tokens and ratios.
- State. Web: Open state is aria-expanded on the trigger. Danger items are marked by colour and by the explicit verb ('Delete …'). Android: The trigger reads Expanded / Collapsed. Danger items use colour plus the verb.
- Motion. Web: The menu appears without animation. Android: The Popup appears without animation.

Known accessibility gaps:
- ContextMenu.tsx: items are 40px tall with no eq-touch, below the 48 minimum target (Compose items are 48dp).

Example: Chat long-press
```tsx
<ContextMenu items={[
  { label: 'Mark as read', icon: 'done-all' },
  { label: 'Call back', icon: 'call' },
  { label: 'Delete chat', icon: 'delete', danger: true },
]} />
```
```kotlin
ContextMenu(
    items = listOf(
        ContextMenuItem("Mark as read", EqualIcons.DoneAll, onClick = {}),
        ContextMenuItem("Call back", EqualIcons.Call, onClick = {}),
        ContextMenuItem("Delete chat", EqualIcons.Delete, onClick = {}, destructive = true),
    ),
)
```

Example: Overflow menu
```tsx
<OverflowMenu items={[
  { label: 'Edit', icon: 'edit', onSelect: edit },
  { label: 'Delete instruction', icon: 'delete', danger: true, onSelect: confirmDelete },
]} />
```
```kotlin
OverflowMenu(
    items = listOf(
        ContextMenuItem("Edit", EqualIcons.Edit, onClick = {}),
        ContextMenuItem("Delete instruction", EqualIcons.Delete, onClick = {}, destructive = true),
    ),
)
```

#### Dialog (`dialog`)

A centred decision dialog with a text cancel and one filled commit, plus the inverse-surface Snackbar that confirms an action afterwards.

- React: `import { Dialog, Snackbar } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `EqualDialog`, `EqualDialogContent`, `EqualSnackbar`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `shadow/nav`, `bg/overlay`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `button/primary`, `button/danger`, `button/secondary`
- Source: Surfaces from the Typography screen inventory · Dialog, Snackbar/Toast

Do: Commit is filled and cancel is a text action, right-aligned (rule 4). Reuse the verb from the control: Turn off → "Turn off" button → "Call learning turned off" snackbar. Offer Undo on the snackbar for reversible deletes.

Don't: Don't write "OK" / "Yes" as the commit; name the action. Don't stack a snackbar on an open dialog.

Anatomy:
1. Scrim: Dims the screen behind the dialog. Tapping it cancels. (bg/overlay · web overlay covers the nearest positioned ancestor · Compose uses a platform Dialog window)
2. Container: Centred surface that holds the decision. (312 wide (max 100% - 48 web) · bg/surface · radius 24 · padding 24 · shadow/nav (web))
3. Title: The question, e.g. 'Turn off Call Learning?'. (title token · text/primary)
4. Subject: Optional line naming what the dialog applies to. (caption · text/secondary · 2 above (web))
5. Body: States the consequence. (body1 · text/secondary · 12 above web / 8 Compose)
6. Actions: Right-aligned text cancel and a filled commit (danger when destructive). (TextButton neutral text/secondary (web), EqualTextButton text/action (Compose) + Button md 36 · gap 20 web / 8 Compose · 24 above)
7. Snackbar: Inverse toast confirming the action afterwards, with an optional text action such as Undo. (fill text/primary · message body1 in bg/surface · radius 12 · padding 12/16 · action button text: button/secondary web, text/action Compose)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: The box is role="alertdialog" (aria-modal in overlay mode) and the title is an h2. Snackbar is role="status". Android: EqualDialog uses a platform Dialog window and the content sets paneTitle. The title is heading(). EqualSnackbar is a polite liveRegion.
- Name. Web: aria-label is the title and aria-describedby points at the body. Button names come from their visible labels. Android: paneTitle is the title. TalkBack reads the content in order; button labels come from their text.
- Keyboard. Web: useModal moves focus to the first button, traps Tab, makes the screen behind inert, cancels on Escape and returns focus on close. A scrim click cancels. Android: The platform Dialog takes focus and Back calls onDismissRequest. TalkBack: swipe between title, body and buttons, double-tap to activate.
- Touch target. Web: TextButton, the md commit Button (36 visual) and the Snackbar action all use eq-touch, so each hit area is 48. Android: EqualButton and EqualTextButton apply minimumInteractiveComponentSize; the Snackbar action has a 48dp minimum too.
- Contrast. Web: Body and subject text/secondary are 5.7:1 on bg/surface, the title 12.6:1. The primary commit is 2.85:1 in light (accepted brand decision); danger is 6.2:1. Snackbar message is 12.6:1; its lime action is 10.5:1 in light but about 1.3:1 in dark, where the fill turns light grey. Android: Same dialog tokens. The Cancel action is EqualTextButton in text/action, green on white 2.85:1 in light (brand green). The Snackbar action uses text/action: green on the #333 fill is 4.4:1 in light, lime on the light-grey fill about 1.3:1 in dark.
- State. Web: Destructive is shown by the danger fill and the verb in the label ('Delete'), not by colour alone. Android: Same: danger variant plus a named verb.
- Motion. Web: The dialog and snackbar have no animation. Android: The platform Dialog window uses the system animation, which follows the system animation scale.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Snackbar action contrast in dark: the fill is text/primary (white 80%, a light grey), so the lime action is about 1.3:1 on web (button/secondary, Dialog.tsx) and Android (text/action, Overlays.kt). In light, the Compose green action on the #333 fill is 4.4:1, just under 4.5.
- Snackbar in Dialog.tsx: role="status" is mounted together with its message, so many screen readers do not announce it. Keep a persistent live region (Announce) and set the text after it exists.
- Accepted brand decision: EqualDialogContent (Overlays.kt) draws Cancel as EqualTextButton in text/action #00B140, 2.85:1 on white in light mode (web uses neutral text/secondary).
- Accepted brand decision: primary buttons put text/on-action white on button/primary #00B140 in light mode, 2.85:1 for 14sp text (Button.css / Buttons.kt). Dark (black on lime) is 17.4:1.

Example: Inline
```tsx
<Dialog open mode="inline" title="Turn off Call Learning?" subject="Call learning"
  body="Your assistant will stop learning from new calls. What it already knows stays until you clear it."
  confirmLabel="Turn off" />
```
```kotlin
// EqualDialogContent is the dialog surface without the window, for inline use
EqualDialogContent(
    title = "Turn off Call Learning?",
    subject = "Call learning",
    body = "Your assistant will stop learning from new calls. What it already knows stays until you clear it.",
    confirmLabel = "Turn off",
    onConfirm = {},
    onDismiss = {},
)
```

Example: Destructive
```tsx
<Dialog open mode="inline" destructive title="Delete address?" subject="Work"
  body="Your assistant will no longer share this address with delivery partners."
  confirmLabel="Delete" />
```
```kotlin
EqualDialogContent(
    title = "Delete address?",
    subject = "Work",
    body = "Your assistant will no longer share this address with delivery partners.",
    confirmLabel = "Delete",
    destructive = true,
    onConfirm = {},
    onDismiss = {},
)
```

Example: Overlay + snackbar
```tsx
<Dialog open={open} title="Turn off Call Learning?" confirmLabel="Turn off"
  onCancel={() => setOpen(false)}
  onConfirm={() => { setOpen(false); setToast('Call learning turned off'); }} />

{toast && <Snackbar message={toast} actionLabel="Undo" onAction={undo} />}
```
```kotlin
var open by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
var toast by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }
EqualButton(text = "Turn off Call Learning", onClick = { toast = null; open = true })
if (open) {
    EqualDialog(
        onDismissRequest = { open = false },
        title = "Turn off Call Learning?",
        subject = "Call learning",
        body = "Your assistant will stop learning from new calls. What it already knows stays until you clear it.",
        confirmLabel = "Turn off",
        onConfirm = { open = false; toast = "Call learning turned off" },
    )
}
toast?.let { EqualSnackbar(message = it, actionLabel = "Undo", onActionClick = { toast = null }) }
```

Example: Snackbars
```tsx
<Snackbar message="Contact saved" />
<Snackbar message="Chat deleted" actionLabel="Undo" onAction={undo} />
```
```kotlin
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)) {
    EqualSnackbar(message = "Contact saved")
    EqualSnackbar(message = "Chat deleted", actionLabel = "Undo", onActionClick = {})
}
```

#### Snooze & update (`snooze`)

Assistant Snooze and Force Update parts: the duration dialog (OK disabled until a choice is made), the alert sheet with its art straddling the top edge, the troubleshooting list, the update art and the spinner that replaces the assistant switch while it turns on or off.

- React: `import { SnoozeDurationDialog, AlertSheet, alertSheets, TroubleshootList, UpdateArt, Spinner } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `SnoozeDurationDialogContent`, `AlertSheet`, `AlertSheets`, `TroubleshootList`, `UpdateArt`, `ForceUpdateScreen`, `EqualSpinner`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `bg/primary`, `bg/overlay`, `button/primary`, `stroke/medium`, `stroke/dark`, `suggest/glow`, `text/secondary`
- Source: Assistant Snooze · Fore Update

Props of `TroubleshootList`:
- `items`: `{ icon: IconName; label: string }[]`. Information-only rows.

Props of `UpdateArt`:
- `size?`: `number` = 160. 160 on the hard update, 144 on the sheet.

Props of `Spinner`:
- `size?`: `number` = 20. Diameter.
- `label?`: `string`. Accessible name; omit when nearby text says what is loading.

Do: Keep OK disabled until a duration is picked. Say why it failed and give the next step on the same sheet. Turning the assistant back on needs no dialog.

Don't: Don't preselect a duration. Don't give the hard update a close button; Back exits the app.

Anatomy:
1. Duration dialog: Pick how long the assistant stays off. (Dialog 312, radius 24, padding 24 · title · body1 secondary · RadioGroup m, gap 20 · Cancel (neutral) + OK md, disabled until a choice)
2. Busy toggle: The assistant card while it turns off or on. (AssistantToggle · 20 Spinner in the 40×24 switch slot · deactivating keeps the on fill, activating the off fill)
3. Alert sheet: Why it failed, and the next step. (radius 32 top · bg/primary · padding 24 / 28 · art centred on the top edge · title · body1 secondary max 292 · lg block CTA · neutral secondary)
4. Troubleshooting list: Things the user can try. (max 272 · radius 12 · 1 stroke/dark · rows 44, icon 18 + body1 · stroke/medium dividers)
5. Update art: The update robot and its badge. (mascot-update 160 / 144 · badge 22.5 % button/primary with a 3 bg/primary ring and arrow_upward · suggest/glow disc behind)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Dialog is role='alertdialog' with a radiogroup; sheets are role='dialog' named by their title; the troubleshooting list is a list. Android: Dialog pane with selectableGroup; sheets set paneTitle; list rows merge descendants.
- Name. Web: Each radio reads its duration; the busy card reads its title ("Deactivating your assistant"). Android: Same; the busy toggle's stateDescription is Busy.
- Keyboard. Web: Arrow keys move through the durations; Tab reaches Cancel and OK; Escape closes dialogs and sheets. Android: D-pad through options and actions; Back closes (except the hard update, where Back exits the app).
- Touch target. Web: Radio rows, buttons and the 44 close are at least 44. Android: 48dp via minimumInteractiveComponentSize; close 44 in a 48 target.
- Contrast. Web: Body text/secondary on bg/primary passes 4.5:1; disabled OK is text/on-action-disabled on button/disabled (disabled is exempt). Android: Same tokens.
- State. Web: OK has the disabled attribute until a choice is made; the busy card is aria-busy with a polite live region on its text. Android: OK enabled = false; the toggle text sits in a polite liveRegion.
- Motion. Web: The spinner and sheet slide-in stop under reduced motion. Android: EqualSpinner and the sheet's enter animation respect rememberReduceMotion().

Known accessibility gaps:
- The heads-up notification in docs is drawn by the DS; on device it is a real NotificationCompat, so its accessibility is the system's.

Example: Duration dialog
```tsx
const [v, setV] = useState<SnoozeDuration | null>(null);

<SnoozeDurationDialog value={v} onChange={setV} onConfirm={snooze} onCancel={close} />
```
```kotlin
var v by remember { mutableStateOf<SnoozeDuration?>(null) }
SnoozeDurationDialogContent(
    selected = v,
    onSelect = { v = it },
    onConfirm = { /* snooze */ },
    onCancel = { /* close */ },
)
```

Example: Alert sheet
```tsx
<AlertSheet {...alertSheets['activation-failed']} onCta={retry} onSecondary={openSupport} onClose={close}>
  <TroubleshootList items={activationFixes} />
</AlertSheet>
```
```kotlin
AlertSheet(
    spec = AlertSheets.ActivationFailed,
    onCta = { /* retry */ },
    onSecondary = { /* support */ },
    onClose = { /* close */ },
) {
    TroubleshootList(ActivationFixes)
}
```

Example: Update art and spinner
```tsx
<UpdateArt size={144} />
<Spinner size={20} />
<Spinner size={32} />
```
```kotlin
UpdateArt(size = 144.dp)
EqualSpinner(size = 20.dp)
EqualSpinner(size = 32.dp)
```

#### System notification (`system-notification`)

The Android heads-up notification Equal AI posts, drawn over the status bar in mocks and flows (e.g. “Equal AI Assistant is back on”).

- React: `import { SystemNotification } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `SystemNotificationPreview`
- Tokens: `component/notification/bg`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/placeholder`
- Source: Flows: Temporarily Unavailable

Do: Keep the title under about 32 characters, so it fits on one line on a 360dp phone.

Don't: Don’t use it as an in-app toast; it stands for the OS notification.

Anatomy:
1. Shell: Rounded heads-up card. (radius xl (20) · padding 12 16 16 · notification/bg · shadow 0 8 28 @14% + 0 1 3 @8%)
2. Header row: App name, dot and time. (Text micro at 10 · text/primary · 3 dot text/placeholder · gap 6)
3. Orb: Equal app icon. (10 above · EqualOrb / EqualLogoOrb 32 · gap 10)
4. Title: Bold first line. (Text caption Bold · text/primary · one line with ellipsis on Compose)
5. Body: Second line. (Text caption Regular · text/secondary)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: role="status" on the shell, so a mock that renders is read politely; the orb is role=img. On a real device the OS draws and announces the notification. Android: No semantics beyond text; in the app the real notification is posted with NotificationCompat.
- Name. Web: Read as app, time, "Equal AI" (orb), title and body; the dot is aria-hidden. Android: App, time, title, body; the orb has contentDescription = null.
- Keyboard. Web: Not interactive. Android: Not interactive in the preview.
- Touch target. Web: Not interactive. Android: Not interactive in the preview; the OS notification handles taps.
- Contrast. Web: Header and title text/primary 12.6:1; body text/secondary 5.7:1 on white (dark 9.7:1 and 6.2:1 on #2A2A2A). Android: Same tokens, same ratios.
- State. Web: No state. Android: No state.
- Motion. Web: The shell has no animation; flows wrap it in .eq-heads-up (slide in, 320 ms), which is off under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: No animation.

Known accessibility gaps:
- The web orb keeps its default label "Equal AI", so screen readers hear the app name twice (header, then orb); Compose passes contentDescription = null (SystemStatus.tsx).

Example: Back on
```tsx
<SystemNotification title="Equal AI Assistant is back on"
  body="Equal AI is now handling all your unknown calls." />
```
```kotlin
// On a device, post a NotificationCompat instead; this preview is for mocks and flows
SystemNotificationPreview(
    title = "Equal AI Assistant is back on",
    body = "Equal AI is now handling all your unknown calls.",
)
```

### Group: You tab

#### AI summary card (`ai-summary-card`)

The "Your AI Summary" card, prose the assistant wrote about the user, with empty, loading and ready states.

- React: `import { AiSummaryCard } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `AiSummaryCard`
- Tokens: `gradient/ai-summary`, `stroke/subtle`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`
- Source: You tab · AI Summary card

Do: Write the summary in the assistant's voice, second person, short sentences. Use the loading state while the summary refreshes rather than hiding the card.

Don't: Don't show a stale summary with a spinner; use `status="loading"`. Don't use bullet lists; the summary is prose.

Anatomy:
1. Card: Soft green-tinted card for the summary. (gradient/ai-summary · radius 20 · padding 16 · min height 212 · gap 12)
2. Header: Orb and label. (orb 28 · caption · text/secondary · gap 8)
3. Body: Empty message, loading skeleton, or the summary prose. (bodyLarge text/primary · empty: Medium, centred)
4. Skeleton: Loading bars that pulse. (5 bars × 17 high · gap 4 · stroke/subtle · 0.95 ↔ 0.45 over 1.4s, staggered 90ms)
5. Footer: 'Last Updated: 8:06 AM' or 'Usually ready after your first few calls'. (caption Regular · text/secondary · right-aligned)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: A div with aria-busy while loading. The orb is role="img". The skeleton is role="status" with aria-label 'Summary is updating'. Android: A plain Column. EqualLogoOrb has contentDescription 'Equal AI'. The loading box has contentDescription = label and stateDescription 'Summary is updating'.
- Name. Web: The orb reads 'Equal AI', then the label 'Your AI Summary', the body and the footer. Android: TalkBack reads 'Equal AI', 'Your AI Summary', the body (or 'Your AI Summary, Summary is updating') and the footer.
- Keyboard. Web: Nothing is focusable. Android: TalkBack: swipe through the texts.
- Touch target. Web: Not interactive. Android: Not interactive.
- Contrast. Web: Body text/primary 12.6:1 or more on the gradient. Label and footer text/secondary are 5.6:1 at the #EAF9EF stop in light and 5.7:1 at #2E3520 in dark. Android: Same tokens.
- State. Web: Loading is exposed through aria-busy and the status region; the footer text also changes to 'Last Updated'. Android: Loading is exposed through stateDescription; the footer text also changes.
- Motion. Web: The skeleton pulses (eq-shimmer). Under reduced motion the base.css rule sets animation-duration to 0ms. Android: The skeleton pulse runs from rememberInfiniteTransition and holds still when rememberReduceMotion() is true.

Known accessibility gaps:
- AiSummaryCard in YouTab.tsx: the loading role="status" is mounted at the same time as the loading state and has no text (only an aria-label), so most screen readers will not announce it. Use a persistent Announce region.

Example: Ready
```tsx
<AiSummaryCard summary="Your family calls you a lot. They always say it's urgent. They almost never say why." />
```
```kotlin
// Compose: status isn't inferred from summary; pass Ready explicitly
AiSummaryCard(
    status = AiSummaryStatus.Ready,
    summary = "Your family calls you a lot. They always say it's urgent. They almost never say why.",
)
```

Example: Empty
```tsx
<AiSummaryCard />
```
```kotlin
AiSummaryCard()
```

Example: Loading
```tsx
<AiSummaryCard status="loading" lastUpdated="8:06 AM" />
```
```kotlin
AiSummaryCard(status = AiSummaryStatus.Loading, lastUpdated = "8:06 AM")
```

#### Contact info header (`contact-info-header`)

The top of the Contact Info screen: a 96dp avatar, name, phone and a row of action tiles (Call, Mute, Save, Share).

- React: `import { ContactInfoHeader } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `ContactInfoHeader`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `stroke/subtle`, `text/action`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`
- Source: Contact Info (Contact Info)

Do: Use the four tiles Call · Mute · Save · Share, with Material Symbols icons in text/action. Flip the Mute tile label to Unmute when the contact is muted.

Don't: Don't add more than four tiles; they share one row. Don't use emoji on the tiles; these are icon tiles, not action chips.

Anatomy:
1. Avatar: Initials avatar with the saved-contact badge, or category art for unknown callers. (ContactAvatar 96dp · initials Medium 36sp in contact-avatar/*-text on contact-avatar/*-bg · person badge 36% of size on contact-avatar/badge-bg)
2. Name: Contact or caller name. (headline at 22/28 Bold · text/primary · centred · 10 above)
3. Phone: Phone number. (bodyLarge · text/secondary · tabular)
4. Action tiles: Row of equal-width tiles: Call, Mute, Save, Share. (72 high · radius 8 · gap 12 · bg/surface · shadow 0 1 2 black/4%, 1dp stroke/subtle in dark · 24 above)
5. Tile icon: Material Symbol for the action. (Icon 24 · text/action)
6. Tile label: Action name; Mute flips to Unmute. (body1 · text/primary · 8 below the icon)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: The name is an h1. Each tile is a <button>, and the icon is aria-hidden. The saved badge is role="img". Android: The name is heading(). Tiles are clickable Columns with Role.Button that merge the icon and label.
- Name. Web: Tiles are named by their label. The category avatar's alt is the category name, and the saved badge's is 'Saved contact'. Initials are read as text. Android: Tiles are named by their label. The category avatar's contentDescription is the category label, and the saved badge's is 'Saved contact'.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab through the tiles, Enter/Space to activate. Android: TalkBack: swipe to a tile, double-tap.
- Touch target. Web: Tiles are 72 tall and about 77 wide in the 390 frame. Android: Tiles are 72dp tall and share the row width.
- Contrast. Web: Name 12.6:1 and phone 5.7:1 on the page. Initials are 4.7–6.5:1 on their tinted discs. Tile icons are text/action #00B140 on white, 2.85:1 in light (accepted brand decision); lime on #1F1F1F is 13.7:1 in dark. Android: Same tokens and ratios.
- State. Web: Mute shows its state through the label (Mute / Unmute), not through colour. Android: Same, via defaultContactInfoActions(muted).
- Motion. Web: Press scale (eq-pressable), 0ms under reduced motion. Android: eqPressFeedback on press.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision: ContactInfoHeader tile icons (Profile.tsx / Profile.kt) are text/action #00B140 on white, 2.85:1 in light, under 3:1 for icons.

Example: Saved contact
```tsx
<ContactInfoHeader name="Amit Nanda" phone="+91 98717 46113" avatar={{ initials: 'AN' }}
  actions={[
    { icon: 'call', label: 'Call' },
    { icon: 'silent-mode', label: 'Mute' },
    { icon: 'person-add', label: 'Save' },
    { icon: 'share', label: 'Share' },
  ]} />
```
```kotlin
ContactInfoHeader(
    name = "Amit Nanda",
    phone = "+91 98717 46113",
    initials = "AN",
    actions = listOf(
        ContactInfoAction("Call", EqualIcons.Call, onClick = {}),
        ContactInfoAction("Mute", EqualIcons.SilentMode, onClick = {}),
        ContactInfoAction("Save", EqualIcons.PersonAdd, onClick = {}),
        ContactInfoAction("Share", EqualIcons.Share, onClick = {}),
    ),
)
```

Example: Unknown caller, with history
```tsx
<ContactInfoHeader name="Arnav Raj" phone="+91 98717 46113"
  avatar={{ category: 'career' }} actions={actions} />
<SectionHeader size="label" inset={22}>Call history</SectionHeader>
<CallHistoryList>
  <CallHistoryRow direction="incoming" meta="Today • 30 Sec." time="02:30 PM" />
  <CallHistoryRow direction="missed" meta="Yesterday" time="11:04 AM" />
</CallHistoryList>
```
```kotlin
ContactInfoHeader(
    name = "Arnav Raj",
    phone = "+91 98717 46113",
    category = EqualCategory.Career,
    // Call · Mute · Save · Share
```

#### Invite card (`invite-card`)

The mint "Invite a Friend" pill at the bottom of the You tab, with the high-five art rising above it and a share button.

- React: `import { InviteCard } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `InviteCard`
- Tokens: `invite/bg`, `invite/stroke`, `bg/surface`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`
- Source: You tab · Invite card

Do: Leave ~29dp of space above the card for the art to rise into. Keep it the last item on the You tab, above the bottom nav.

Don't: Don't rotate the art again; the tilt is baked into the file. Don't crop the high-five illustration to fit the card.

Anatomy:
1. Card: Mint pill near the bottom of the You tab. (invite/bg · 1dp invite/stroke · radius 24 · min height 68 · padding 10/6/10/108 · gap 12 · 32 above, 16 below (web))
2. High-five art: 3D illustration rising above the card, flush left. (Asset illustration-high-five 113×112 · 29 above the card top · tilt baked in · decorative)
3. Title: 'Invite a Friend'. (subheading · text/primary · truncates)
4. Subtitle: 'Invite Friends To Join'. (caption Regular · text/secondary · truncates)
5. Share button: Pill button that opens sharing. (56×40 · radius full · bg/surface · share 22 · text/secondary · 48 touch height)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: A div. Share is a <button>. The art is <img alt="">. Android: A Box. Share is a clickable Box with Role.Button. The art has contentDescription null.
- Name. Web: Share's aria-label is 'Share invite'. Android: The share icon's contentDescription is 'Share invite'.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to Share, then Enter/Space. Android: TalkBack: swipe to 'Share invite', double-tap.
- Touch target. Web: Share is 56×40 with eq-touch, so the hit area is 56×48. Android: Share is a 56×40dp visual inside touchTarget(), giving 56×48dp.
- Contrast. Web: Title text/primary 12.4:1 and subtitle text/secondary 5.7:1 on invite/bg (9.7 and 6.2:1 in dark). The share icon text/secondary on bg/surface is 5.7:1 (6.7:1 dark). Android: Same tokens.
- State. Web: No states. Android: No states.
- Motion. Web: Press scale only (eq-pressable), 0ms under reduced motion. Android: Press indication only.

Example: Default
```tsx
<InviteCard onShare={shareInvite} />
```
```kotlin
InviteCard(onShare = {})
```

Example: Custom copy
```tsx
<InviteCard title="Give a month free" subtitle="Share Equal AI with family" onShare={shareInvite} />
```
```kotlin
InviteCard(title = "Give a month free", subtitle = "Share Equal AI with family", onShare = {})
```

#### Plan card (`plan-card`)

The dark card showing the user's current plan (Equal AI UNLIMITED, ₹149/Monthly), with a Manage plan action and an expired state.

- React: `import { PlanCard } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `PlanCard`
- Tokens: `plan-card/bg`, `plan-card/pill-stroke`, `plan-card/pill-bg`, `gradient/unlimited-text`, `plan-badge/expired-stroke`, `gradient/expired-badge`, `plan-card/pattern`, `text/on-dark`, `text/on-dark-secondary`, `text/accent-gold`, `text/danger`
- Source: You tab · Plan card

Do: Show the price with the period ("₹149/Monthly"); it renders in tabular figures. Use the expired state with Manage plan so renewing is one tap.

Don't: Don't replace the coded gold pattern with an image. Don't place the plan card on a white surface; it belongs in the gold hero.

Anatomy:
1. Card: Dark card for the current plan. (plan-card/bg #2E2E2E · radius 20 · padding 14/16/16)
2. PlanPattern: Coded stepped gold lines on the right side. (right 60% · plan-card/pattern · stroke 0.9 · fades 0 → 0.55 → 0.8 · decorative)
3. Status pill: 'Current Plan', or 'Plan Expired' on a red sheen. (24 high · radius 8 · padding 0 10 · 1dp plan-card/pill-stroke · plan-card/pill-bg · caption text/on-dark · expired: gradient/expired-badge over plan-card/expired-pill, 1dp plan-badge/expired-stroke)
4. Manage plan: Underlined text action. (buttonSmall · text/on-dark · underline · 48 touch area)
5. Product and tier: 'Equal AI UNLIMITED' with the tier painted in gold. (title · text/on-dark · tier gradient/unlimited-text (text/accent-gold fallback on web) · 12 above)
6. Price: Price and period, e.g. '₹149/Monthly'. (caption Regular · text/on-dark-secondary · tabular)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: A plain div. Manage plan is a <button>. The pattern SVG is aria-hidden. Android: A Box. Manage plan is a clickable Box with Role.Button. The pattern Canvas has no semantics.
- Name. Web: Manage plan is named by its label (actionLabel, default 'Manage plan'). Android: Named by manageLabel.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to Manage plan, then Enter/Space. Android: TalkBack reads the pill, product, tier and price, then 'Manage plan, button'.
- Touch target. Web: Manage plan uses eq-touch, giving at least 48. Android: Manage plan sits inside touchTarget(), giving a 48dp area.
- Contrast. Web: On #2E2E2E: text/on-dark 13.6:1, text/on-dark-secondary 5.9:1, the gold tier 6.0:1 or more. The Current Plan pill is 14.9:1. The expired pill's white text sits over the light middle of gradient/expired-badge (#E4918C), about 2.4:1. The card looks the same in both themes. Android: Same tokens and ratios.
- State. Web: Expired shows as the text 'Plan Expired' as well as the red fill. Android: Same: the label changes to expiredLabel.
- Motion. Web: None. Android: None.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Expired status pill (YouTab.css .eq-plan__pill.is-expired / PlanCard in YouTab.kt): white caption text over gradient/expired-badge drops to about 2.4:1 at its #E4918C middle, below 4.5:1.

Example: Current and expired
```tsx
<PlanCard onManage={managePlan} />
<PlanCard status="expired" onManage={managePlan} />
```
```kotlin
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)) {
    PlanCard(onManageClick = {})
    // Compose: status="expired" is a Boolean flag
    PlanCard(expired = true, onManageClick = {})
}
```

Example: Custom tier
```tsx
<PlanCard tier="LITE" price="₹49/Monthly" />
```
```kotlin
PlanCard(tier = "LITE", price = "₹49/Monthly")
```

#### Profile hero (`profile-hero`)

The gold header at the top of the You tab (avatar, name, plan marker, edit, phone) that hosts the plan card, plus the compact ProfileHeader.

- React: `import { ProfileHero, ProfileHeader } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `ProfileHero`, `ProfileHeader`
- Tokens: `gradient/profile-hero`, `gradient/gold`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`
- Source: You tab · Profile hero

Do: Put the PlanCard inside the hero as children so it sits on the gold. Drive `avatar` from the gender chosen in Personal Details.

Don't: Don't add more actions to the hero row; edit is the only one. Don't format the phone number without tabular figures.

Anatomy:
1. Hero background: Gold gradient header with two faint arcs (ProfileHeroArcs). In dark mode it becomes a panel with rounded bottom corners. (gradient/profile-hero · arcs r250/r290, 1.2 stroke, white 55% · padding 20 top, 12 sides · dark: radius 24 bottom, ends 56 above the bottom)
2. Plain tone: No-plan header: flat mint panel, no arcs, no plan badge or card. (profile-hero/plain-bg · radius 20 bottom · padding 20/12 · follows the theme)
3. Avatar: ProfileAvatar: the gold-ringed avatar for paid users; the plain tone draws the bust on a green disc in a green ring. (70dp (paid) · plain: 71×80 box, 5dp button/primary ring, 58 button/primary disc, bust 58)
4. Name: User's name. (headline · text/primary (light tokens in both themes on gold) · truncates)
5. Plan badge: Plan marker, e.g. UNLIMITED. (PlanBadge · 16 high · radius 4 · padding 0 6 · gradient/gold · badge token text/on-dark · gap 8)
6. Edit button: Opens profile editing. (28dp · edit-profile 18 · text/primary web, text/secondary Compose · 48 touch area)
7. Phone: Phone number. (body1 · text/secondary · tabular)
8. Footer slot: Holds the PlanCard so it sits on the gold. (16 below the row)
9. ProfileHeader: Compact version without the gold background. (avatar 56 · gap 16 web / 12 Compose · padding 16 web · headline + PlanBadge · phone body1 text/secondary)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: A <section>. The name is an h1, the arcs and the plain avatar are aria-hidden, and Edit is an IconButton (<button>). Android: Plain Column. The name is heading(). Edit is a Box with Role.Button. The plain avatar is cleared from semantics.
- Name. Web: The hero avatar is decorative (label=""). Edit is 'Edit profile'. ProfileHeader's avatar keeps alt 'Your profile'. Android: ProfileAvatar in the gold row reads 'Your profile'. Edit's icon contentDescription is 'Edit profile'.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab reaches Edit, then Enter/Space. Android: TalkBack: swipe to 'Edit profile', double-tap.
- Touch target. Web: Edit is 28px with eq-touch, giving a 48 area. Android: Edit is a 28dp visual inside touchTarget(), giving a 48dp area.
- Contrast. Web: The gold row renders with light tokens in both themes (data-theme="light"): name 10.7:1 and phone 5.3:1 at the #F5E4AE top. The plain tone is 12.2 and 5.7:1 in light, 10.8 and 6.7:1 in dark. The UNLIMITED badge is white on gradient/gold, 3.0–4.2:1 at 10sp. Android: The row renders under EqualTheme(darkTheme = false), so the ratios match web in both themes, badge included.
- State. Web: Plan shown as badge text, e.g. 'UNLIMITED'. Android: Plan shown as badge text.
- Motion. Web: None, apart from the eq-pressable press scale on Edit, which is 0ms under reduced motion. Android: None, apart from the press indication.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Accepted brand decision (premium gold, subscription surfaces only): planBadge (Badge.css / Badges.kt): white 10sp text on gradient/gold (#A37236 → #B58D55) is 3.0–4.2:1, below 4.5:1.

Example: You tab hero with plan card
```tsx
<ProfileHero name="Keshav" phone="+91 98789 56749" onEdit={editProfile}>
  <PlanCard onManage={managePlan} />
</ProfileHero>
```
```kotlin
ProfileHero(name = "Keshav", phone = "+91 98789 56749", onEdit = {}) {
    PlanCard(onManageClick = {})
}
```

```tsx

```
```kotlin

    name = "Priya Sharma",
    phone = "+91 99100 22114",
    avatar = ProfileAvatarVariant.Female,
    plan = null,
    onEdit = {},

```

```tsx
<ProfileHeader name="Keshav" phone="+91 98789 56749" />
```

#### Settings & promos (`settings-promos`)

Call Learning cards (what the assistant learns, with an example), the Account & Data trust strip, the Teach Your Assistant promo and the generic new-feature sheet.

- React: `import { LearningCard, TrustStrip, InstructionsPromoCard, FeatureIntroSheet } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `LearningCard`, `TrustStrip`, `InstructionsPromoCard`, `FeatureIntroSheet`
- Tokens: `preset/tint-orange`, `preset/tint-lime`, `preset/tint-green`, `glass-button/default`, `trust-strip/bg`, `instructions-promo/bg`, `instructions-promo/title`, `instructions-promo/cta`
- Source: Profile · Preset Instruction

Props of `LearningCard`:
- `emoji`: `string`. 56 tile.
- `tint`: `'orange' | 'lime' | 'green'`. Card tint.
- `title`: `string`. body2 600.
- `body`: `string`. Why.
- `example`: `ReactNode`. Italic example in the glass box.

Props of `TrustStrip`:
- `stats`: `{ art; value; label }[]`. Three stats.

Props of `InstructionsPromoCard`:
- `title / body / cta?`: `string` = Teach Your Assistant…. Copy (experiments).
- `onCta / onDismiss?`: `() => void`. Actions.

Props of `FeatureIntroSheet`:
- `hero`: `ReactNode`. Tinted top.
- `title`: `string`. Headline.
- `bullets`: `{ icon; text }[]`. Icon rows.
- `cta`: `string`. Primary.
- `secondary?`: `string`. Text button.
- `badge?`: `string` = 'New feature'. Soft badge.

Do: Give each learning card a concrete example. Let the promo be dismissed.

Don't: Don't use the teal promo tint for anything but Instructions.

Anatomy:
1. Learning card: One thing the assistant learns. (radius 16 · preset tint · 56 emoji tile · body2 600 title · caption body · italic example in glass-button/default)
2. Trust strip: Why to trust Equal. (radius 20 · trust-strip/bg · three 40 art stats with stroke/medium dividers)
3. Promo: Teach Your Assistant. (radius 18 · instructions-promo/bg · title 700 instructions-promo/title · 32 pill CTA · 96 mascot)
4. Feature intro sheet: A new feature explained. (radius 28 top · tinted hero · soft badge · headline 600 · 20 icon bullets · lg CTA + text secondary)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Cards are articles; the sheet is a dialog; the promo CTA and close are buttons. Android: Same; the sheet sets paneTitle.
- Name. Web: Card titles are headings; the sheet is named by its title. Android: Headings on titles.
- Keyboard. Web: The carousel scrolls with Shift+wheel or Tab into each card; Escape closes the sheet. Android: D-pad; Back closes the sheet.
- Touch target. Web: Promo CTA 32 high in a 44 target. Android: 48dp.
- Contrast. Web: Promo title #0F766E on #EAF7F5 5.0:1; CTA white on #0F766E 5.5:1. Android: Same tokens.
- State. Web: None. Android: None.
- Motion. Web: The sheet slide is off under reduced motion. Android: Same.

Example: Call Learning cards
```tsx
{learningCards.map((c) => <LearningCard key={c.title} {...c} />)}
```
```kotlin

```

Example: Trust strip
```tsx

```
```kotlin

```




## Flows (27)

### Monetization (`/flows/monetization`)

Equal Unlimited: the free-plan touchpoints that open the paywall, the paywall itself, payment results, managing and cancelling the plan, and lapsed plans. The Android team experiments here, so every screen takes the experiment knobs (price, coupon, copy, entry touchpoint) as props.

Source: Monetization Flow

1. Touchpoints (where the paywall opens from): locked rows in the chat list (blurred preview, crown-lock), a locked conversation (Unlock All Details), locked audio (Unlock Audio), Manage plan on the You tab’s plan card, and the Reactivate banners on a lapsed plan. They sit on the revamped screens as props: HomeScreen lockedFrom, ChatScreen lock (details · audio · lapsed) and YouScreen plan (none · active · restore · reactivate). Pass the entry as touchpoint so the paywall previews what the user was trying to see.
2. Paywall: gold hero with the crown, “Unlock Equal Unlimited”, the price under LIMITED TIME DISCOUNT, the preview card, the EQUAL25 coupon (APPLY → APPLIED drops ₹249 to ₹149), FAQ, and the sticky gold Unlock Unlimited with “Cancel Anytime. Automatically renews”.
3. Payment: Waiting for Confirmation (auto) → Payment Confirmed (redirect in 5s) → Congratulations (redirect to home). Pending offers Contact Support; Failed offers Retry Payment; both say the refund comes within 24 hours. Support opens the Help Center sheet.
4. After: the home header shows UNLIMITED and avatars turn gold. The You tab’s plan card has Manage plan → the subscription page (plan end date, 400k+, rating, testimonials, FAQ).
5. Cancel: tell us why (Proceed disabled until there is text) → are you really sure (Cancel / Confirm) → request submitted (redirect in 3s). Access stays until the end date; the page then offers Re-Subscribe.
6. Lapsed: the You tab shows Restore Plan or Reactivate plan with the amber banner; chats show “Reactivate your current Plan to keep using Equal Unlimited”.
7. Experiments (props, not forks): price / discountedPrice (₹249, ₹149), coupon (none · available · applied), subtitle (“Unlock Summaries…” · “Get Unlimited Summaries…”), touchpoint (chat-list · chat · audio), waitingArt (coin · cash), HomeScreen lockedFrom (how many free chats).

States:
- `home-free` Home, free plan (locked chats): `<HomeScreen tier="free" lockedFrom={4} promo="meet-assistant" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      // Free plan: rows from index 4 on are locked; tapping one opens the paywall
      HomeScreenSample(
          tier = PlanTier.Free,
          lockedFrom = 4,
          promo = { MeetAssistantCard(onCallClick = {}, onDismiss = {}) },
          onLockedChat = { /* open PaywallScreen(touchpoint = PaywallTouchpoint.ChatList) */ },
      )
  }
  ```
- `chat-locked` Chat: Unlock All Details: `<ChatScreen lock="details" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      // Free plan: bubbles blurred, recording locked, Unlock All Details instead of the AI panel
      ChatScreenSample(lock = ChatLock.Details, onUnlock = { /* open PaywallScreen(touchpoint = PaywallTouchpoint.Chat) */ })
  }
  ```
- `chat-audio` Chat: Unlock Audio: `<ChatScreen lock="audio" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      // Free plan: only the call summary recording is locked (Unlock Audio)
      ChatScreenSample(lock = ChatLock.Audio, onUnlock = { /* open PaywallScreen(touchpoint = PaywallTouchpoint.Audio) */ })
  }
  ```
- `paywall` Paywall (Try it: apply, unlock): `<PaywallScreen touchpoint="chat-list" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      // Live: APPLY drops ₹249 to ₹149; Unlock → Waiting → Confirmed → Welcome
      PaywallScreen(touchpoint = PaywallTouchpoint.ChatList)
  }
  ```
- `paywall-chat` Paywall from a chat: `<PaywallScreen touchpoint="chat" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      PaywallScreen(touchpoint = PaywallTouchpoint.Chat)
  }
  ```
- `paywall-audio` Paywall from audio, coupon applied: `<PaywallScreen touchpoint="audio" coupon="applied" subtitle="get" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      PaywallScreen(touchpoint = PaywallTouchpoint.Audio, coupon = PaywallCoupon.Applied, subtitle = PaywallSubtitle.Get)
  }
  ```
- `waiting` Waiting for Confirmation: `<PaywallScreen overlay="waiting" />`
  ```kotlin

      PaywallScreen(overlay = PaywallOverlay.Waiting)
  }
  ```
- `confirmed` Payment Confirmed: `<PaywallScreen overlay="confirmed" />`
  ```kotlin

      PaywallScreen(overlay = PaywallOverlay.Confirmed)
  }
  ```
- `pending` Payment Pending: `<PaywallScreen overlay="pending" />`
  ```kotlin

      PaywallScreen(overlay = PaywallOverlay.Pending)
  ```

- `failed` Payment Failed: `<PaywallScreen overlay="failed" />`

### Assistant health check (`/flows/health-check`)

Checks that calls really reach the assistant: app permissions, phone settings and the carrier. Every failure comes with the one action that fixes it. Switch to Try it and run the live check.

Source: Assistant Healthcheck

1. Entry: a notification (“Calls are bypassing Equal AI. Fix now.”, with Fix Now / Notify Later), the pink “Poor Assistant Health · Fix Now →” strip under the assistant toggle on Home, or You → Assistant Health Check.
2. Permissions: Start Health Check runs Phone, Notification and Contacts one at a time. A missing one turns its ring red; the group then offers Grant Permission, which opens Android’s page for each.
3. Phone settings: the same for Overlay (display over other apps).
4. Carrier: checks calls reach the assistant. Issues Found → Fix Now → Fixing; if the fix fails, the reasons and Try Again; if the check itself fails, Check Failed and Try Again.
5. All good: the shield gets its check, “Check complete. Your assistant is good to go”, Back To Home. The hero is the supplied Lottie set (loading, check, cross and every transition between them).

### Assistant snooze (`/flows/snooze`)

Turning the assistant off asks how long for; it comes back on by itself at that time, or when the user turns it on. Every failure says why and offers the next step. Switch to Try it and run it live.

Source: Assistant Snooze

1. Turn off: tapping the switch while On opens “Want to deactivate assistant?”. Nothing is preselected and OK stays disabled until a duration is chosen. Cancel, the scrim or Back leaves it On.
2. Deactivating: the switch becomes a spinner (“This will take just a moment…”), then Off with “Equal will be back Today 6:45pm” and the heads-up “Equal AI Assistant is off”.
3. Turn back on: no dialog. Activating (“Resuming on your Equal AI Assistant”), then On.
4. Errors: airplane mode or no internet (Go to settings · Try Again), any other snooze failure (Try again), and activation failure with the troubleshooting list (Try now · Contact Support). Closing a sheet leaves the assistant as it was.

States:
- `on` On: `<SnoozeFlow state="on" />`
  ```kotlin

      SnoozeFlowSample(initial = "on")
  }
  ```

  ```kotlin
      SnoozeFlowSample(initial = "dialog-empty")

  ```

  ```kotlin

      SnoozeFlowSample(initial = "dialog-selected")
  }
  ```
- `deactivating` Deactivating: `<SnoozeFlow state="deactivating" />`

### Force update (`/flows/force-update`)

On start or resume the app checks its version. Below the minimum supported version it blocks with a full-screen update; when a newer version exists it offers a dismissible sheet.

Source: Fore Update

1. Hard: installed &lt; minimum supported. Full screen, no close; Back exits the app. Update Equal AI opens the Play Store (or an in-app IMMEDIATE update).
2. Soft: a newer version exists. “A new version is here” over Chats; Update Now (in-app FLEXIBLE update) or Maybe Later / ✕ / scrim / Back to dismiss it for this version.

States:
- `hard` Hard update: `<ForceUpdateScreen onUpdate={openPlayStore} />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      ForceUpdateSample(hard = true, onUpdate = { /* open the Play Store / IMMEDIATE update */ })
  }
  ```
- `soft` Soft update: `<AlertSheet {...alertSheets['update-available']} onCta={update} onSecondary={later} onClose={later} />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      ForceUpdateSample(hard = false, onUpdate = { /* FLEXIBLE update */ }, onLater = { /* snooze this version */ })
  }
  ```

### Known call usage cap (`/flows/usage-cap`)

Free users share a weekly allowance between known and unknown calls, and each type has its own cap. Home shows what is left; a gold sheet rises once at 20 %, at 100 % and at each cap; View Details explains the split. The card has three experiment options (A, B, C).

Source: Known Call Usage Cap

1. Home card: “67 Calls left this week”, a known / unknown meter, the reset. From 20 % used an Upgrade Now appears (A in the header, B and C full width, C in gold).
2. Limit sheets: each rises over Home once per week per threshold (20 %, 100 %, known cap, unknown cap). Close or the scrim dismisses it; the CTA opens the paywall.
3. View Details: View Details (A) or the chevron (B, C) opens the green sheet: calls left, per-type meters, the reset and the perks or the info note.
4. Numbers are props: the total, the per-type caps and every count. The design’s numbers disagree in places (68 + 12 vs 68 + 18, a 30-call protection limit); product decides the real ones.

### Equal to Equal call (`/flows/equal-call`)

An Equal user calls another Equal user over the internet. The receiver sees who is calling, identified by Equal, wherever the phone is; the caller calls from the chat and can minimise to a strip.

Source: Equal To Equal Call Experience

1. Receiver, ringing: locked → the full-screen call (Decline · swipe up to Accept · Message). Unlocked → Android’s heads-up (DECLINE / ANSWER). Swiped away while Equal is open → the in-app strip at the top of Chats (three options as a prop; option 1 is the one that passes AA in light).
2. Connecting → Connected: the initials disc gains ripples, “Connected” and the timer; speaker, mute and end in the bar. Minimise shows the ongoing strip (mute · name and time · end); tapping it returns.
3. Caller: the call icon in the chat → “Let’s get you talking” the first time → Android’s dialog → Calling… → Ringing… → Connected. Not now or Deny stays in the chat.
4. After: the chat shows the ongoing strip while the call is live (the call icon disabled), then a Voice Call card with the duration.

States:
- `receiver-lock-ringing` Receiver: locked, incoming: `<EqualCallReceiverFlow stage="lock-ringing" />`
  ```kotlin

      EqualCallReceiverSample(stage = ReceiverStage.LockRinging)
  ```

### Home, You and settings updates (`/flows/home-you-updates`)

The Updated UI screens that were missing: an empty and an offline Home, the new chat-row states, the Settings notice on You, Splash, Call Learning & Consent, Account & Data, and the Teach Your Assistant promo.

Source: Updated UI · Profile · Preset Instruction

1. Home: a new user sees “Your chats will appear here”; offline shows the no-internet state instead of the list. Rows can be missed by the assistant, on a call (the Ongoing call pill), without chips, loading their summary, or muted.
2. Turning the assistant off asks how long for: see the Assistant snooze flow. Indefinitely off reads “Assistant is resting.”
3. You: a dismissible notice says settings moved into You.
4. Account & Data builds trust (the shield and three stats) and leads to Call Learning & Consent, where turning learning off asks first. The Figma’s second red row reuses the Call Learning copy; it is shown here as Delete account (flag for design).
5. Teach Your Assistant sits in the home carousel; Try Instructions opens the new-feature sheet.

States:

### AI personalisation (`/flows/personalisation`)

Equal learns how you handle each caller and says what it noticed. Home introduces it once, the You tab shows “Equal Noticed…”, AI Personalization explains what is and isn’t learned, and each caller has a context card you can pause or delete.

Source: About Me (Notice Card) & AI personalization

1. Introduce: a sheet on Home says Equal is getting to know your callers, what it ignores, and that it can be off for anyone.
2. You tab: the first time, a coach mark points at “Updated summary is ready · Tap to reveal”; then “Equal Noticed…” with thumbs and when it updates. Several summaries become a carousel. AI Personalisation opens the screen.
3. AI Personalization: what Equal picks up, what it never saves (OTPs, card numbers, UPI PINs, IDs), excluded contacts, and Delete all learning (What stays / What goes).
4. Per caller: Contact Info shows Equal’s context for that person. Its menu stops personalising (it keeps what it knows, learns nothing new; Resume brings it back) or deletes the learning.
