### Call your assistant (vOIP) (`/flows/voip`)

Meet Your Assistant → “Call me” starts an in-app call with the assistant over the internet. The mic is asked for in two steps; if the user says no at either, the assistant phones them the normal way instead.

Source: vOIP

1. Call me: the Meet Your Assistant card on Home. If the mic is already allowed, the call connects straight away.
2. Mic: an in-app prompt first (“Talk to your assistant”, Not now / Allow microphone), then Android’s own dialog. Not now or Deny → the assistant calls on the phone network (PSTN) instead.
3. On the call: the assistant on the green disc with ripples, “Connected” and a running timer. Speaker and mute are independent switches; mute changes the status to “On mute”.
4. End: “Call ended” with the final time, then back to Home after 2 s. Not designed yet: back during a call, connect failure, and the action card left in the chat.

States:
- `home` Home: Call me: `<VoipFlow />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      VoipFlowSample()
  }
  ```
- `mic-prompt` Mic, in-app prompt: `<VoipFlow stage="mic-prompt" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      VoipFlowSample(stage = VoipStage.MicPrompt)
  }
  ```
- `mic-system` Mic, Android dialog: `<VoipFlow stage="mic-system" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      VoipFlowSample(stage = VoipStage.MicSystem)
  }
  ```
- `connecting` Connecting: `<VoipFlow stage="connecting" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      VoipFlowSample(stage = VoipStage.Connecting)
  }
  ```
- `connected` Connected: `<VoipFlow stage="connected" seconds={1} />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      VoipFlowSample(stage = VoipStage.Connected, seconds = 1)
  }
  ```
- `speaker` Speaker on: `<VoipFlow stage="connected" speaker seconds={1} />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      VoipFlowSample(stage = VoipStage.Connected, speaker = true, seconds = 1)
  }
  ```
- `muted` On mute: `<VoipFlow stage="connected" muted seconds={5} />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      VoipFlowSample(stage = VoipStage.Connected, muted = true, seconds = 5)
  }
  ```
- `ended` Call ended: `<VoipFlow stage="ended" seconds={155} />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      VoipFlowSample(stage = VoipStage.Ended, seconds = 155)
  }
  ```
- `pstn` Fallback: phone call: `<VoipFlow stage="pstn" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      VoipFlowSample(stage = VoipStage.Pstn)
  }
  ```

### Temporarily unavailable (`/flows/system-status`)

What Chats shows while Equal AI is down, and how it tells you it’s back. Switch to Try it and tap “Notify me when ready” to run the whole flow.

Source: Temporarily Unavailable

1. Unavailable: the System status card takes the assistant toggle’s place, with the sleeping robot and an amber “Notify me when ready”. The promo card is hidden while the system is down.
2. Notify requested: the pill becomes a green “✓ You’ll be notified soon”. Nothing else on the screen changes.
3. Back on: a heads-up notification (“Equal AI Assistant is back on”) drops in, the toggle returns as “AI Assistant is On”, and Meet Your Assistant with “Call me” sits above Conversations.

### Instructions flow (`/flows/instructions`)

The hub, presets, the “Setting up instruction” chat and Active Instructions. Switch to Try it and apply an instruction end to end.

Source: Instructions

1. Hub: horizontal recommended cards with a tinted + Apply (or “New suggestions coming…” once they’re all applied), the Active Instructions row with the robot-with-wand art, three presets led by their 3D art, and a pinned “Add New Instruction”.
2. Preset: the description plus instruction cards with WHEN / DO pills and + Apply, which turns into Applied.
3. Setup chat, no input: You → Equal AI “Got it! Here’s your instruction:” → preview → ✍️ Edit / 👍 Confirm. Confirm adds ✅ and saves.
4. Setup chat, input needed: Equal AI asks each follow-up (the landmark, then the wait time); the answers are bolded in the preview → ✏️ Change something else / 👌 That’s all.
5. Active: cards with the preset’s source badge, WHEN / DO, and ⋮ Edit / Delete instruction; plus an empty state.
6. In the chat: after a call, the summary says which instructions ran: “🪄 2 instructions applied in this call”.

### Plan value & renewal (`/flows/plan-renewal`)

Before a plan ends, show what it did for the user, then make renewing one tap. Home carries the expiry strip, a call near the end brings up the What Unlimited saved you sheet, and Manage plan leads to the renewal page and the paywall.

Source: Monetization value, Monetization local components

1. Expiry strip under the home header: amber “Your Plan Expires in 2 Days”, red “Expires Today” and “Expired on 30th July”, each with Renew Now. Pass planExpiry to HomeScreen; nothing shows while the plan is comfortably active.
2. Value sheet once called: after the assistant handles a call near the end of the plan, the What Unlimited saved you sheet rises over home: calls handled, three perks, the expiry chip (03 Days amber, Today / 30th July red) and the current plan, with Renew your Equal AI. Close floats above the sheet. valueSheet="flush" is the experiment where the card is the sheet. In dark mode the card turns black with a gold glow.
3. Free plan quota: the same sheet for free users counts the week’s calls. Under the limit it reads “6 out of 30 Calls Left” with a gold progress bar; at the limit, “Limit Reached · 30 out of 30 (100%)”. Both show when the quota resets and Subscribe to Equal AI Unlimited at ₹149, with Get Equal AI Unlimited opening the paywall. Pass quotaSheet to HomeScreen.
4. Plan card: active shows Current Plan; expired shows the red Plan Expired pill and a plain avatar. Manage plan opens the plan page either way.
5. Plan page: Equal AI Unlimited hero, What Unlimited Saved You (calls, plan active until or expired on, price), What You Get, social proof and FAQ. The plan action is pinned: Cancel Subscription (gold outline) while active, Renew your Equal AI once expired, which opens the paywall with Get Equal AI Unlimited.
6. Motion (local components): APPLY strikes the old price, lands the new one with the list price and “Saved ₹100”, and pops the Special Coupon Applied! badge. The gold CTA has a sheen sweep. The waiting sheet steps through Connecting To Razorpay → Waiting for Confirmation → Verifying Transaction, then Payment Confirmed with the ray burst behind the seal. Everything holds still under reduced motion.

States:
- `home-expiring` Home: expires in 2 days: `<HomeScreen planExpiry={{ state: 'expiring', days: 2 }} promo="meet-assistant" />`
  ```kotlin

      )
  ```


### Global MYA (`/flows/global-mya`)

Tap the green orb anywhere and your assistant answers in a sheet: a greeting, quick actions and suggestions, then a request typed or spoken. The request turns into a short task conversation that ends with the result to confirm.

Source: Global MYA

1. Open: the green orb (the nav FAB) opens the sheet over whatever screen you’re on: orb, “Good morning, Keshav” (name in green), “What can I help you with today?”, three quick-action tiles, suggestion chips, and a message field with the mic.
2. Type: focusing the field hides the tiles and lifts the input above the keyboard (green outline). Enter sends.
3. Speak: the mic swaps the field for Send voice note with a keyboard toggle. Tap it to record: “Try saying …”, then delete, the timer with a live waveform, and send. Or press and hold: “Release to send, slide left to cancel”, and sliding left turns the waveform red (“Release to cancel”).
4. Task: once sent, the sheet grows into a conversation titled with what the assistant is doing (“Setting up a reminder…”), with close. Your voice note (player + transcript) → Thinking… → the result card (here a WhatsApp reminder) with Edit / Confirm.
5. Inside a chat: the chat’s own AI layer (“Want me to send Amit a quick reply on WhatsApp?”) works the same way. Tapping a chip or sending a message raises the task sheet, which stops below the chat header so you can still see whose chat it is. “Replying Amit on WhatsApp” shows the drafted reply with ✏️ Edit / 📤 Send and the 📤 Send · ✏️ Edit draft · 🖋️ Custom chips. Confirming shows “Opening WhatsApp…” and greys the chips out.
6. Done: Confirm ticks the card, the sheet closes, and the chat it acted on now reads “Reminder added”. Saved contacts carry the person badge on their initials.

States:
- `home` Home (Try it: tap the orb): `<HomeScreen chats={chats} promo="meet-assistant-carousel" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      // Home: tap the green orb (nav FAB) to open the live sheet
      HomeScreenSample(chats = MyaSampleChats, promo = { MeetAssistantCarousel(onDismiss = {}) })
  }
  ```
- `greeting` Greeting & quick actions: `<HomeScreen chats={chats} assistantResult={{ chatId: 'c3', preview: 'Reminder added' }} />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      HomeScreenSample(chats = MyaSampleChats, promo = { MeetAssistantCarousel(onDismiss = {}) }, assistant = MyaStage.Greeting)
  }
  ```
- `chat-ai` In a chat: the AI layer (Try it): `<ChatScreen chat={amit} />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      // Tap Reply on WhatsApp (or send a message) to open the task sheet
      ChatScreenSample(name = "Amit Nanda", initials = "AN", category = EqualCategory.NA, subtitle = "+91 98717 46113")
  }
  ```
- `chat-task` In a chat: Replying Amit on WhatsApp: `<ChatScreen chat={amit} aiTask="draft" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      ChatScreenSample(name = "Amit Nanda", initials = "AN", category = EqualCategory.NA, subtitle = "+91 98717 46113", aiTask = ChatTaskStage.Draft)
  }
  ```
- `chat-sending` In a chat: Opening WhatsApp: `<ChatScreen chat={amit} aiTask="sending" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      ChatScreenSample(name = "Amit Nanda", initials = "AN", category = EqualCategory.NA, subtitle = "+91 98717 46113", aiTask = ChatTaskStage.Sending)
  }
  ```

### Monetization touchpoints (`/flows/monetization-touchpoints`)

Where a free user meets Equal Unlimited. Each touchpoint is an experiment option the Android team A/B tests, built as props on the same Home, Chat and Paywall screens.

Source: Plan Expired Touchpoint · Usage Cap Touchpoint (options 1 & 2) · Touchpoint: Actions on Home Page · Recordings + Transcripts Locked (with / without actions) · Component 25

1. Plan expired, option 1: the red PLAN EXPIRED badge, and Equal AI’s own verified chat on top (“Your Plan Expired…”, 👑 Renew Now). Its message is a voice note plus Renew Equal AI Unlimited, which opens the paywall previewing a locked summary.
2. Plan expired, option 2: no chat, a card under the header instead (👑 Your Plan Expired · Renew Now).
3. Usage cap: the assistant switches Off at the weekly limit. Option 1 is again an Equal AI message (“Weekly call limit reached…”). Option 2 is a meter card: “7 Calls left this week · Resets Mon | Unlimited on premium” with Get Unlimited.
4. Actions locked: action chips turn gold with the crown-lock. Tapping one opens the paywall (here the sheet) with “Unlock Unlimited Actions…” and the locked row as its preview.
5. Plan expired, option 3: on the You tab the plan card says Expired and asks to renew, with a gold Renew Equal AI Unlimited.
6. iOS parity paywall: a warm hero (animated or still crown), the black “Limited time deal” price card, the coupon, the locked summary and a black CTA.
7. Recordings locked, options 1 and 2: an Equal AI message (“Your call recordings are locked”) or a home card (Call Recordings Locked · Get Unlimited), with or without the icon.
8. Recordings locked: bubbles blur, the recording washes gold under the crown-lock, and Unlock All Details sits at the bottom. With actions, Call Back / Add to Calendar stay visible under the summary and show locked in the paywall preview.
9. Toggle art (Component 25): the phone-with-sparkles is an experiment on the toggle; the robot stays the default.

States:
- `expired-home` Plan expired 1: Equal AI chat: `<HomeScreen tier="free" planExpired official="plan-expired" />`

### Sheet paywall & payment (`/flows/paywall-sheet`)

The experiment that opens the paywall as a sheet over the screen the user was on, offers EQUAL25 when they try to leave, and shows full-screen payment results. If the user closes a pending payment, every surface says it is processing and the paywall locks.

Source: Light / Dark Mode: Home Screen · Conversation Screen · All Payment States · Payment Pending: Home Screen · If User Closes the payment pending page · Dark Mode_Monetization

1. Sheet: a compact gold card (crown, Equal AI Unlimited, “Trusted by 10 Lakh+ Indians”, ₹249, EQUAL25 · APPLY) with Unlock Equal AI Unlimited. Support opens the Help Center FAQ sheet, and back returns.
2. Exit offer: tapping outside asks Leave Without Unlocking? “Claim 25% off with EQUAL25 first, go Unlimited for ₹149/month.” On home the buttons read Not Now / Claim 25% Off; in a chat, Leave / Keep 25% Off. Claim reopens the sheet at ₹149 with APPLIED. Not Now closes it and leaves the Go unlimited for ₹149 with EQUAL25 · Claim Now strip on home.
3. Results are full screens on a tinted wash with rings. Congratulations, You’re Unlimited, shows Plan active till. Payment Pending has × and Refresh Status, or Contact Support. Payment Failed has ‹ and suggests another UPI app, with Retry payment and Contact Support.
4. Closed while pending: a “Payment processing · We’ll update your order once it’s confirmed.” strip under the chat header and as a card under the home toggle. On the paywall it’s a toast above a disabled Unlock Unlimited, so nobody pays twice.
5. Dark mode: everything follows the theme switch (black and gold paywall, deep green / brown / red result washes, lime buttons).

States:
- `sheet` Sheet paywall (Try it): `<HomeScreen tier="free" paywallSheet="sheet" />`

### Call Handling (`/flows/call-handling`)

You → Your assistant → Call Handling: which calls the assistant answers and who always rings you. New users are invited into it from home: two questions, one minute. The wording is an experiment, so the question screen takes a copy prop.

Source: Known Calls (new users)

1. Where it lives: You → Your assistant → Call Handling (“Choose which calls I answer”). New users see the “Talk With Your Assistant” home, then the dark Set up your calls takeover: “Two questions. One minute.”
2. Question 1: “Which calls should I answer? You decide. I follow.” Two radio cards: All calls, except a few and Only unknown numbers. The copy experiment (copy="whose") asks “Whose calls should I answer?”, tags All calls as ⭐ Suggested, and says what each option means for your contacts.
3. All calls: needs the contacts permission (sheet: “I need your contact list to know who is calling.”) and offers call history so frequent callers sort first. Then Anyone you want to answer yourself?: search, suggested people, all contacts with checkboxes and an A–Z index; the button counts the picks. Ends on Perfect! naming who will always ring you.
4. Only unknown numbers: ends on All Sorted! (“Your contacts will ring you, like always.”). Without the permission, All calls is dimmed and a blue note offers Give contacts permission ›.
5. Later: if the user stops halfway, home shows Finish your setup? with Finish or Skip, answer everyone. Always ring me edits the list; with no saved contacts, Direct Calls explains why it’s empty. The hero art on the contact screens is also a Lottie (call-handling-contacts).

States:
- `home-new` Home, new user: `<CallHandlingScreen />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      // No chats yet: the search field hides and the hero promo fills the home
      HomeScreenSample(
          chats = emptyList(),
          promo = { MeetAssistantHero() },
          assistantDescription = "Equal is managing your calls!",
      )
  }
  ```
- `exclude` Exclude contacts: `<CallHandlingScreen step="exclude" picked={[]} />`

### Known-call notifications (`/flows/known-calls`)

When the assistant answers someone you know, Android shows an ongoing notification that tells you who it is and what they want, with quick replies, and hands the call to you when it needs you. Opening it shows the live chat.

Source: Known-call notifications

1. Answering: “Equal AI • Ongoing” with a live timer; the caller (their avatar) and “Your Equal AI is answering your call.”, with the Equal app badge.
2. Summary: the line updates to what the caller wants as the call goes on.
3. Expanded: two lines, a call button to pick up, and quick replies: Takeover first, then suggested answers the assistant can say for you.
4. Hand-off: when it needs you, the replies give way to “This needs your attention, connecting this call to you”.
5. Open: the chat shows the call live under a black Ongoing call - 02:34 strip with Takeover in the header and the assistant’s follow-up below. Android draws the notification shell; the system wallpaper here is a coded stand-in.

States:
- `answering` Answering: `<CallNotification name="Mom" state="answering" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      CallNotification(name = "Mom", state = CallNotificationState.Answering)
  }
  ```

  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      CallNotification(name = "Mom", state = CallNotificationState.Summary, summary = SampleCallSummary)
  }
  ```
- `expanded` Expanded: quick replies: `<CallNotification name="Mom" state="expanded" replies={["Takeover", "I’ll bring them all", "I’ll call back to get more"]} onReply={reply} onAnswer={answer} />`
  ```kotlin

      CallNotification(
          name = "Mom",
          state = CallNotificationState.Expanded,
          replies = listOf("Takeover", "I’ll bring them all", "I’ll call back to get more"),

  ```
- `connecting` Needs you: connecting: `<CallNotification name="Mom" state="connecting" />`

- `chat` Live chat: `<ChatScreen chat={mom} live ongoing="02:34" />`

### Search (`/flows/search`)

Search from home: names, numbers, categories and keywords across calls. Results arrive in two passes, chats first and messages after, so something useful shows while the slower search finishes.

Source: Search

1. Open: tapping “Search for names” on home opens search with the keyboard up. The bar is a green-outlined pill with back inside it.
2. Before typing: recent searches show as avatar tiles with Clear all. With none, the robot and “Search across your calls · Look for names, phone numbers, categories, keywords”.
3. Typing: green dots under CHATS, then matching chats (with their action chips). Messages load next under MESSAGES, each hit showing who, when, and the line with the match in bold.
4. Nothing found: the thinking robot, “No results found”, and a nudge to try another name, number, category or keyword.
5. Offline: the struck-through wifi, “No internet connection”. The same art works anywhere the network is needed.

States:
- `empty` Empty: `<SearchScreen keyboard state="empty" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      // keyboard = true draws the system keyboard stand-in (docs only)
      SearchScreen(state = SearchState.Empty, keyboard = true)
  }
  ```
- `offline` No internet: `<SearchScreen keyboard state="offline" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      SearchScreen(state = SearchState.Offline, keyboard = true)
  }
  ```

  ```kotlin

      // Live: type to run loading → chats → messages
      SearchScreen(keyboard = true)
  }
  ```

### Call Back (`/flows/call-back`)

The AI layer calls someone back for you: it suggests what to ask, hands off to the phone’s dialer, and leaves an Outgoing call card in the chat.

Source: Call Back

1. Prompt: “Want me to give a quick call back to the clinic?” with 📞 Call Back, 🗓️ Add to Calendar and 🔔 Set reminder chips.
2. Task sheet: “Calling Dr. Mehta’s Clinic” (stops below the chat header). The assistant lists what to ask (reports, location, charges, insurance) with 📞 Call Back.
3. Hand-off: the phone’s own dialer places the call; the system draws it, so the docs show a coded stand-in.
4. Result: an Outgoing call card (“You called back Dr. Mehta’s Clinic · Bring previous medical reports”) with 📞 Call back.
5. From a missed call: when the assistant couldn’t pick up, the thread shows a missed-call card instead of a summary. With a reason: the caller’s art with a missed badge, “LIKELY CALLS FOR …” and 👍/👎. With only a name: “Valluri Called”. With nothing: “Missed by the assistant”. Its Call back opens the same task.

States:
- `live` Chat (Try it: tap Call Back): `<ChatActionScreen action="call-back" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      // Runs live from the chat: tap the chip, then follow the task sheet
      ChatActionScreen(action = ChatAction.CallBack, onBack = { /* pop */ })
  }
  ```
- `ask` Calling: what to ask: `<ChatActionScreen action="call-back" step="ask" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      ChatActionScreen(action = ChatAction.CallBack, step = "ask", onBack = { /* pop */ })
  }
  ```
- `dialer` Dialer (system, stand-in): `<ChatActionScreen action="call-back" step="dialer" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      ChatActionScreen(action = ChatAction.CallBack, step = "dialer", onBack = { /* pop */ })
  }
  ```
- `done` Back in the chat: `<ChatActionScreen action="call-back" step="done" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      ChatActionScreen(action = ChatAction.CallBack, step = "done", onBack = { /* pop */ })
  }
  ```
- `missed-reason` Missed call: with reason (Try it): `<ChatActionScreen action="call-back" missed="reason" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      // The card's Call back opens the ask step
      ChatActionScreen(action = ChatAction.CallBack, missed = MissedCase.Reason, onBack = { /* pop */ })
  }
  ```
- `missed-name` Missed call: name only: `<ChatActionScreen action="call-back" missed="name" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      // The card's Call back opens the ask step
      ChatActionScreen(action = ChatAction.CallBack, missed = MissedCase.Name, onBack = { /* pop */ })
  }
  ```
- `missed-unknown` Missed call: caller unknown: `<ChatActionScreen action="call-back" missed="unknown" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      // The card's Call back opens the ask step
      ChatActionScreen(action = ChatAction.CallBack, missed = MissedCase.Unknown, onBack = { /* pop */ })
  }
  ```

### Mute (`/flows/mute`)

Muting a caller from the chat: the assistant double-checks, because muting means missing their calls even when they matter.

### Reply on WhatsApp (`/flows/reply-whatsapp`)

The assistant drafts a WhatsApp reply from the call. The user sends it as is or edits it in place, WhatsApp opens with the message entered, and the chat keeps a record.

Source: Reply On WhatsApp

1. Draft: “Replying Amit on WhatsApp”: You “Reply on whatsapp”, then the draft with ✏️ Edit / 📤 Send.
2. Edit: “Edit Message” dims the chat and floats the draft above the keyboard. The bubble grows with the text (about 11 lines, then scrolls); the green check saves.
3. Send: “send as is” → Opening WhatsApp…, chips grey out; WhatsApp opens with the message entered.
4. Confirmation: “Wrote a draft for Amit” and a WhatsApp card with the message and 👀 View message.

### Save Contact (`/flows/save-contact`)

Saving an unknown caller as a contact from the chat, including editing the details, the contact form, and every path through the contacts permission.

Source: Save Contact

1. Prompt: “This number isn’t saved. Add Rahul to your contacts?” with 👤 Save contact.
2. Review: “Saving contact”: the pre-filled card (Rahul (Electrician), number) with ✏️ Edit / 💾 Save and “Looks right? Tap Save to add them.”
3. Edit: by voice (“What should I change?”, Hold to speak) or in the contact form. Two forms are on the table: iOS-revamp parity (grouped rows) and exact WhatsApp parity (outlined fields, Sync contact to phone).
4. No permission: a centred dialog “Allow contacts permission · Open Settings”. Back from Settings, the chat offers ▶️ Continue saving. If granted, the pre-filled card returns with ✏️ Edit / 👍 Confirm; if not, a “Contact Permission Required” card with ⚙️ Open Settings.
5. Saved: “Saved! Rahul is in your contacts now.” with 👤 View contact.

States:
- `live` Chat (Try it): `<ChatActionScreen action="save-contact" />`

### Error states (`/flows/error-states`)

How the AI layer fails: say what happened in one line and offer the one action that fixes it.

Source: Error states

1. Generation failure: “Sorry, I couldn’t do that just now. Please try again.” with 🔄 Retry, inside the task.
2. Offline in a task: “It looks like you’re offline. Try again once you’re back online.” with 🔄 Retry.
3. Voice input failure: the AI layer asks again: “Sorry, I didn’t catch that. Could you hold and speak again?”
4. Offline sheet: over the chat, the struck wifi, “No internet connection” and Refresh. Full screen: the same with Try again, when there is nothing to show yet.

States:
- `generation` Generation failure: `<ChatErrorScreen state="generation" onRetry={retry} />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      ChatErrorScreen(state = ErrorState.Generation, onRetry = { /* retry */ })
  }
  ```
- `offline-reply` No internet (in a task): `<ChatErrorScreen state="offline-reply" onRetry={retry} />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      ChatErrorScreen(state = ErrorState.OfflineReply, onRetry = { /* retry */ })
  }
  ```
- `voice` Voice input failure: `<ChatErrorScreen state="voice" />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      ChatErrorScreen(state = ErrorState.Voice)
  }
  ```
- `offline-sheet` No internet (sheet): `<ChatErrorScreen state="offline-sheet" onRetry={refresh} />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      ChatErrorScreen(state = ErrorState.OfflineSheet, onRetry = { /* refresh */ })
  }
  ```
- `offline-screen` No internet (full screen): `<ChatErrorScreen state="offline-screen" onRetry={retry} />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      ChatErrorScreen(state = ErrorState.OfflineScreen, onRetry = { /* retry */ })
  }
  ```

### Contact info (`/flows/contact-info`)

The caller’s page: category avatar, name and number, four action tiles and the call history.

Source: Contact Info

1. Header: a 96dp category avatar (or initials for saved contacts), the headline name and a tabular phone number.
2. Actions: Call, Mute (toggles to Unmute), Save and Share as 72dp tiles with the icon in text/action.
3. Call history: phone_callback, phone_missed (red icon, label not red) and phone_forwarded rows inside a card.

States:
- `contact` Contact Info: `<ContactInfoScreen onBack={goBack} />`
  ```kotlin
  EqualTheme {
      ContactInfoScreen(name = "Amit Nanda", phone = "+91 9871746113", onBack = {})
  }
  ```
